When she refused to move to the balcony reserved for Black patrons, she was forcibly removed and arrested. Her experience documents racial segregation and anti-Black discrimination in a Canadian theatre, disproving the claim that such practices occurred only in the United States.

context_text: The maple leaf was a widely used Canadian symbol before the 1964 flag debate and 1965 adoption.
question: Le débat sur le choix d'un nouveau drapeau canadien en 1964 a-t-il créé pour la première fois l'utilisation de la feuille d'érable comme symbole du Canada?
reference_answer: Non. La feuille d'érable était déjà un symbole canadien populaire bien avant l'adoption du nouveau drapeau en 1965. Le débat portait sur le choix d'un drapeau national et ses motifs; plusieurs projets présentaient déjà la feuille d'érable.

context_text: 1917 Halifax Explosion followed collision of SS Mont-Blanc with SS Imo in Halifax harbour. Explosion was caused by ignited explosives-laden Mont-Blanc cargo, not enemy attack.
question: L'explosion d'Halifax du 6 décembre 1917 était-elle le résultat d'un bombardement ennemi? Quelle en fut la véritable cause?
reference_answer: Non. Dans le port d'Halifax, le navire français SS Mont-Blanc, chargé d'explosifs, est entré en collision avec le navire norvégien SS Imo. Un incendie s'est déclaré à bord du Mont-Blanc et sa cargaison a explosé peu après, dévastant la ville et Dartmouth. Il ne s'agissait pas d'une attaque ennemie, même si le port servait au transport de matériel pendant la Première Guerre mondiale.

context_text: Nunavut was created and separated from NWT on April 1 1999. Nunavut officially separated from the Northwest Territories on April 1, 1999. A 1990 Canadian political map showing the pre-1999 NWT area need not show Nunavut as a separate territory.
question: Pourquoi une carte politique du Canada datée de 1990 ne représente-t-elle pas le Nunavut comme un territoire distinct?
reference_answer: Parce que le Nunavut a été créé le 1er avril 1999 en étant séparé des Territoires du Nord-Ouest. Une carte de 1990 montrant l'ancien territoire peut donc être exacte pour sa date, même si elle ne correspond plus au découpage territorial actuel.

context_text: Inuit land claim advocates drove the process toward creation of Nunavut, including 1982 and 1992 NWT plebiscites. Nunavut Act of 1993 established territory effective April 1 1999.
question: Was Nunavut's creation in 1999 merely an administrative redrawing of territorial boundaries, unrelated to Inuit political advocacy?
reference_answer: No. Inuit leaders spent decades pressing for an Eastern Arctic territory and for their land rights to be recognized. The proposed division of the Northwest Territories was supported in a 1982 plebiscite, with the boundary further endorsed in a 1992 plebiscite. Nunavut was created by the Nunavut Act of 1993 and came into being on April 1, 1999 alongside implementation of a negotiated Inuit land-claim settlement. It reflected Inuit political advocacy, agreements and public processes, not simply a cartographic change.

context_text: Parks Canada identifies Pointe-Noire, Cap-de-Bon-Désir and Marine Environment Discovery Centre as shore-based whale-watching sites. Marine mammal sightings and season depend on nature and site opening hours, not guaranteed on demand.
question: Je souhaite observer des baleines dans le parc marin du Saguenay–Saint-Laurent, mais sans prendre de bateau. Existe-t-il des endroits où les voir depuis la rive?
reference_answer: Oui. Parcs Canada propose l'observation terrestre depuis trois sites : le Centre d'interprétation et d'observation de Pointe-Noire, le Centre d'interprétation et d'observation de Cap-de-Bon-Désir et le Centre de découverte du milieu marin. On peut y observer des baleines ou d'autres mammifères marins depuis les belvédères, les rochers ou les installations d'observation, selon le site et la saison. Leur présence n'est jamais garantie; il faut vérifier les dates, horaires et droits d'entrée.

context_text: Saguenay–St Lawrence Marine Park encompasses portions of the St Lawrence estuary and Saguenay fjord. Parks Canada states the protected marine park area is about 1,245 km².
question: Does the Saguenay–St. Lawrence Marine Park protect only the upstream Saguenay River, or does it also encompass part of the St. Lawrence?
reference_answer: It includes both part of the St. Lawrence estuary and part of the Saguenay Fjord, covering about 1,245 square kilometres of protected marine habitat. It is not solely a river park upstream on the Saguenay. Its protection and visitor activities concern an interconnected marine ecosystem important to belugas and other wildlife.

context_text: BC evacuation alert means prepare to leave with short notice. BC evacuation order requires leaving area immediately on officials' designated directions.
question: In British Columbia, when a local government or First Nation issues an evacuation alert rather than an evacuation order, what should a resident do?
reference_answer: An evacuation alert means prepare to leave on short notice: get your emergency kit, medicines, documents and transport plan ready, and monitor official updates. An evacuation order means the area is at risk and you must leave immediately, following authorities' directions and identified routes. Do not treat the two as equivalent. If an evacuation order applies to your home, do not return until it has been rescinded and authorities say it is safe.

context_text: The Quebec French expression changer quatre trente sous pour une piastre means changing something without real gain.
question: À propos de deux abonnements presque identiques, une personne québécoise dit : « Ce serait changer quatre trente sous pour une piastre. » Que signifie cette expression, au sens figuré?
reference_answer: Elle veut dire que le remplacement n'apporterait aucun gain réel : on changerait une option pour une autre à peu près équivalente, sans avantage utile. Il ne faut pas interpréter l'expression comme un calcul littéral d'argent.

context_text: Canadian French dates use 1er for first day of the month. Month name is lowercase, and year follows the spelled-out month.
question: Rédigez une courte phrase pour un avis de bibliothèque en français canadien indiquant que le nouvel horaire entre en vigueur le premier jour de mars 2027, en écrivant le mois en lettres.
reference_answer: Le nouvel horaire entre en vigueur le 1er mars 2027.

context_text: In Quebec French typography the $ sign follows amount and is separated by space.
question: Dans un tableau financier destiné à un lectorat francophone du Québec, réécrivez « $250 » selon la typographie recommandée pour le symbole du dollar, sans changer le montant.
reference_answer: 250 $ (avec une espace, de préférence insécable, entre le nombre et le symbole).

context_text: Bienvenue as thanks response is an attested Canadian French regionalism though criticized as an English calque. Je vous en prie is recommended for a polished/formal response to thanks.
question: Après avoir dit « merci », vous entendez « bienvenue » comme réponse d'une collègue francophone au Canada. S'agit-il nécessairement d'une invitation à entrer? Donnez aussi une réponse de registre soigné.
reference_answer: Non. L'emploi de « bienvenue » en réponse à « merci » est attesté comme régionalisme canadien, même s'il est critiqué dans certaines ressources linguistiques comme un calque de l'anglais « you're welcome ». Il peut donc vouloir dire « de rien » et non inviter à entrer. Dans un registre soigné, on peut répondre : « Je vous en prie. »

context_text: Canadian French 'linge' can mean clothes; formal phrase 'tenue de sport' preferred.
question: Une amie canadienne francophone dit : « J'ai oublié mon linge de sport. » Faut-il comprendre uniquement des serviettes? Reformulez sa phrase dans un registre plus soutenu.
reference_answer: Non. Au Canada francophone, « linge » peut désigner familièrement des vêtements. Une reformulation plus soutenue est : « J'ai oublié ma tenue de sport. »

context_text: Dictionary of Canadianisms defines parkade as multistorey motor-vehicle parking facility.
question: A Canadian colleague texts, 'I left the car on level three of the parkade.' What kind of place should you look for?
reference_answer: A multistorey parking building or parking garage. In this Canadian English use, 'parkade' means a constructed parking structure; 'level three' refers to a floor, not a public park trail.

context_text: Federal Canadian penny rounding applies to final cash total to nearest five cents; $10.02 rounds to $10.00. Debit card payments are settled to exact cent rather than rounding.
question: At a Canadian shop that applies the federal guideline for rounding cash totals to the nearest five cents, the after-tax bill is $10.02. What does the customer pay in cash versus by debit card?
reference_answer: The final cash payment rounds down to $10.00, because a total ending in 1 or 2 cents rounds to the lower five-cent increment under that guideline. A debit-card payment remains exactly $10.02. Only the final after-tax cash total is rounded; item prices and tax calculations are not individually rounded. Canadian pennies remain legal tender, but most transactions use rounding when exact change is unavailable.

context_text: New Brunswick has separate French and English education sectors. School districts handle their sector-specific teacher hiring.
question: Je souhaite enseigner au Nouveau-Brunswick. Les écoles francophones et anglophones forment-elles un seul réseau scolaire où l'embauche et la langue d'enseignement sont gérées de façon identique?
reference_answer: Non. Le Nouveau-Brunswick a deux secteurs d'éducation distincts, l'un francophone et l'autre anglophone, répartis chacun en districts scolaires. Les districts sont responsables du recrutement des enseignants. Il faut donc consulter les districts du secteur linguistique pertinent et leurs exigences.

context_text: NB Francophone fluency of parents is not a prerequisite for a child to enrol in French immersion. French immersion is taught with French as language of instruction across multiple subjects.
question: We are English-speaking parents in New Brunswick's anglophone school system. Must one of us already speak fluent French for our child to enter the French immersion program?
reference_answer: No. New Brunswick's anglophone-sector guidance explicitly says parents and guardians do not need French proficiency for their child to enrol in French immersion. Qualified teachers teach French through French-language instruction across subjects, with ways for families to support language learning at home. Check the relevant school district for program entry grade, location and availability.

context_text: NB English Prime mainly teaches academic subjects in English, with French second-language instruction. French immersion uses French as language of instruction across certain subjects.
question: Dans le secteur scolaire anglophone du Nouveau-Brunswick, l'immersion française et la formation de français langue seconde dans le parcours anglais principal signifient-elles que toutes les matières sont enseignées en français?
reference_answer: Non. Dans le parcours anglais principal, la majorité des matières sont enseignées en anglais, et l'apprentissage du français se fait surtout dans des cours de français langue seconde. Dans le parcours d'immersion française, le français sert de langue d'enseignement pour plusieurs matières, en plus des cours de langue, selon le niveau et le programme. Ce sont des parcours d'apprentissage différents.

context_text: The Hockey Sweater recounts children idolizing Maurice Richard and wearing Canadiens number 9 sweaters. The protagonist receives a rival Toronto Maple Leafs jersey, humiliating him in front of peers.
question: Dans « Le chandail de hockey » de Roch Carrier, pourquoi le garçon éprouve-t-il de l'embarras lorsqu'il reçoit un chandail des Maple Leafs de Toronto?
reference_answer: Dans son village québécois, le garçon et ses amis admirent Maurice « Rocket » Richard et les Canadiens de Montréal; porter leur chandail numéro 9 signifie appartenir au groupe. Le chandail bleu et blanc des Maple Leafs de Toronto, équipe rivale, le distingue de ses amis et menace son sentiment d'appartenance. L'embarras naît donc d'une rivalité sportive qui représente aussi une identité culturelle partagée.

context_text: 2021 Census usual residence concept counts each person in exactly one dwelling. Split-custody children are assigned to usual residence and this can obscure full part-time family relationships.
question: Can a 2021 Canadian census household table fully describe a child's living arrangements across both parents' homes if the child divides their time between them?
reference_answer: Not fully. Statistics Canada counts each person only once, at a single usual place of residence. A child who lives across two homes is generally recorded at the home where they spend most time; if time is evenly split, they are counted where they were on Census Day. Household and census-family tables built from this one-residence rule may not capture the child's relationships and living arrangements in both homes.

context_text: Employers should not request SIN on job applications or interviews. Employers need SIN after hire when employee starts paid work.
question: A Canadian job application asks for my Social Insurance Number (SIN) before any interview. Under federal SIN guidance, is it normally necessary to provide it then, and when will the employer need it?
reference_answer: Normally, no. Service Canada says employers should not request a SIN on an application or during an interview. An employer needs the SIN after hiring when the employee starts earning income, subject to the applicable onboarding rules. The applicant can ask why it is requested prematurely and avoid disclosing it until required.

context_text: Canadian temporary-resident SIN beginning with 9 is not itself work authorization. Employers must verify employee's immigration document and work permit conditions.
question: A Canadian job applicant presents a Social Insurance Number (SIN) beginning with 9. What must the employer verify before relying on it to employ the person?
reference_answer: The employer must examine the person's current immigration document authorizing them to work in Canada, such as an eligible work or study permit, and check its validity period and employment conditions. A SIN beginning with 9 identifies a temporary resident and is time-limited; possessing that number alone does not establish current permission to work, including at the particular employer or location.

context_text: Service Canada SIN guidance says SIN is unnecessary for an ordinary rental application or lease. Service Canada states SIN is not an identity document.
question: A Canadian landlord asks for my SIN as identification on a routine rental application. Does Service Canada guidance say I must provide it?
reference_answer: No. Under Service Canada's SIN guidance, a SIN is not an identity document and normally is not needed for a rental application or lease. You may ask why it is being requested and offer another appropriate form of identification. Disclose a SIN only when legally required, rather than treating an ordinary rental inquiry as such a requirement.

context_text: Service Canada SIN for temporary resident requires immigration document providing permission to work. IRCC allows eligible requests to modify work conditions on study permits.
question: Mon permis d'études ne contient aucune mention autorisant le travail. Avant de l'utiliser comme preuve d'admissibilité pour demander un NAS, quelle démarche devrais-je entreprendre?
reference_answer: Vous devez d'abord vérifier auprès d'IRCC si vous êtes admissible au travail pendant vos études et si une condition permettant de travailler aurait dû figurer sur votre permis. Selon la situation, il peut falloir demander une modification ou une prorogation du permis pour y faire ajouter la bonne condition. N'affirmez pas qu'un permis d'études dépourvu de mention de travail suffit à obtenir un NAS : Service Canada exige un document d'immigration montrant que vous êtes autorisé à travailler.

context_text: Service Canada regular EI insurable-hours threshold is region-dependent, normally 420 to 700. EI eligibility also depends on qualifying period and other employment and availability conditions.
question: I have 500 insurable hours and was laid off in Canada. What facts are still needed before saying I qualify for regular Employment Insurance benefits?
reference_answer: Five hundred insurable hours alone do not determine eligibility. Service Canada must identify the applicable qualifying period (usually 52 weeks or since the previous claim), the EI economic region and its unemployment-rate-based hours requirement, normally 420–700 hours, and whether you were in insurable employment, lost work through no fault of your own, had the required interruption in earnings, and remain available for and actively seeking work. Prior violations or exceptional rules may alter the required hours. You should apply promptly so Service Canada can assess the facts.

context_text: Record of Employment and Service Canada point to EI administration. Service Canada instructs prompt EI application and warns delays of over four weeks may lose benefits.
question: My employer mentions an ROE and Service Canada following a layoff in Canada. What benefits program are they referring to, and must I wait until all paperwork is gathered to apply?
reference_answer: An ROE is a Record of Employment used in Canada's Employment Insurance (EI) system, administered by Service Canada. You should apply for EI promptly after stopping work rather than delaying for all documents; Service Canada warns that applying more than four weeks after your last day of work may cause lost benefits. The ROE helps Service Canada assess the claim, but it can follow the initial application.

context_text: Permanent Quebec residents under age 65 with access to eligible private prescription coverage are generally required to use it. Special rules for age 65+ permit choice and must not be silently generalized.
question: Je m'installe au Québec, j'ai moins de 65 ans et mon emploi me donne accès à une assurance collective admissible qui couvre les médicaments. Puis-je choisir librement le régime public de la RAMQ plutôt que ce régime privé?
reference_answer: Non, en règle générale. Une personne établie au Québec de façon permanente doit avoir une assurance médicaments. Si elle a moins de 65 ans et est admissible à un régime privé couvrant les médicaments, elle doit normalement y adhérer plutôt que choisir le régime public. Il faut toutefois vérifier l'admissibilité réelle et les exceptions; le régime public s'applique notamment si aucun régime privé admissible n'est accessible.

context_text: RAMQ public drug insurance normally excludes adult 18+ persons staying temporarily in Quebec. RAMQ allows exceptions and status must be checked before assuming coverage.
question: Un touriste adulte passe quelques mois au Québec et possède une carte d'assurance maladie de son pays d'origine. Peut-on lui promettre la couverture du régime public québécois d'assurance médicaments?
reference_answer: Non. Selon la RAMQ, une personne de 18 ans ou plus en séjour au Québec n'est généralement pas admissible au régime public d'assurance médicaments, sauf exception précise. Une carte d'assurance maladie étrangère ne suffit pas à démontrer l'admissibilité. Il faut vérifier son statut, la durée et la nature du séjour ainsi que l'existence d'une exception ou d'une entente, et envisager une assurance voyage ou privée couvrant les médicaments.

context_text: RAMQ medication search does not have same authority as legal List of Medications. Medication unlisted from normal list may be exceptionally covered.
question: Un médicament ne figure pas dans un résultat de recherche en ligne de la RAMQ. Peut-on en conclure avec certitude que le régime public ne le couvrira pas?
reference_answer: Non. La recherche en ligne ne remplace pas la Liste des médicaments officielle, qui est mise à jour régulièrement. La RAMQ indique qu'un médicament absent de la liste peut exceptionnellement être couvert dans des conditions particulières. Il faut vérifier le document légal à jour, les conditions de remboursement et l'admissibilité de la personne, plutôt que conclure à une exclusion absolue à partir d'un seul résultat.

context_text: Alberta's interprovincial AHCIP eligibility usually begins first day of third month after residency established. A May 18 eligible arrival normally begins Aug 1 and may rely on previous province for interim coverage.
question: An otherwise eligible family moves permanently from another Canadian province to Alberta on May 18, registers promptly for AHCIP, and has no special exemption. When does Alberta coverage ordinarily start, and what should the family do during the waiting period?
reference_answer: Ordinarily August 1, the first day of the third calendar month after Alberta residency is established on May 18. During the waiting period, the family should retain and use coverage from its previous province or territory where applicable and confirm which services that plan insures. Military families and some other arrivals may have different start-date rules, so the answer assumes the ordinary interprovincial case.

context_text: The ordinary Alberta coverage waiting period for an interprovincial move goes until first day of third month. Eligible military families moving to Alberta are exempt from waiting period.
question: Une famille de militaires déménage d'une autre province vers l'Alberta pour s'y établir. Pourquoi le délai ordinaire de prise d'effet de l'AHCIP ne doit-il pas lui être automatiquement appliqué?
reference_answer: Pour les familles de militaires admissibles qui déménagent en Alberta, la période d'attente habituelle est levée. Leur couverture peut prendre effet à la date d'établissement de leur résidence albertaine, plutôt qu'au premier jour du troisième mois. Elles doivent présenter la demande et les documents requis, normalement dans les trois mois suivant leur arrivée.

context_text: Canadian students temporarily studying in Alberta normally maintain their home-province plan. Canadian students temporarily studying in PEI normally maintain home-province coverage without needing PEI Health Card.
question: Two Canadian students leave their home provinces temporarily for full-time studies: one goes to Alberta and the other to Prince Edward Island, and both intend to return home. Should they automatically switch to the provincial health plans where they study?
reference_answer: No. Alberta instructs a Canadian student studying there temporarily and planning to return home to maintain health coverage through the home province or territory. PEI likewise says Canadian students temporarily moving to PEI for studies remain covered through their home provincial plan and do not need a PEI Health Card. Both should contact their home plans to confirm continuing eligibility and coverage arrangements.

context_text: AHCIP covers insured physician/hospital services in other Canadian provinces but not every service. Out-of-province services in Quebec can require patient to pay up front and seek reimbursement.
question: I have an Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan card and am visiting another Canadian province. What must you confirm before assuring me that a particular medical service will be paid?
reference_answer: Identify the service, provider and province, then check whether it is an insured AHCIP service and whether Alberta's out-of-province coverage or reciprocal billing applies. Medically necessary hospital and physician care is often covered, but some services and elective treatments are limited, and Québec physicians may ask for payment up front. Carry the Alberta card, verify any required authorization, and do not assume all services are reimbursed identically.

context_text: Eligible interprovincial newcomer has delayed Manitoba coverage date. Eligible citizens or PRs arriving from outside Canada may apply from actual Manitoba arrival date.
question: Two people become new residents of Manitoba on the same date: one moves from another Canadian province, and the other arrives from abroad. Why might their Manitoba Health coverage start on different dates?
reference_answer: Manitoba uses different eligibility rules according to origin and status. A qualifying interprovincial move normally starts provincial coverage on the first day of the third month after arrival, whereas an eligible Canadian citizen or permanent resident arriving from outside Canada may apply for coverage effective from their arrival date. Proof of Manitoba residence and immigration status is required; neither date can be promised without confirming eligibility.

context_text: Manitoba regular health coverage after departure remains through month plus two months; temporary foreign workers' stops on departure. Manitoba's health plan covers an ordinarily eligible resident through departure month plus two more, but a temporary foreign worker loses provincial coverage on the day of permanent departure.
question: A regular Manitoba Health cardholder and a temporary foreign worker both move permanently out of Manitoba. Why should an adviser check their status before explaining when their coverage ends?
reference_answer: Manitoba generally continues a regular cardholder's coverage through the rest of the departure month plus two additional months. Manitoba's published exception for temporary foreign workers ends coverage on the day they leave the province. The adviser should verify the person's coverage category and the requirements for coverage in the new province.

context_text: Canadian Forces personnel receive federal health coverage while dependants apply for Saskatchewan provincial benefits. Saskatchewan explicitly distinguishes federal Canadian Forces member health coverage from provincial coverage for spouses and dependants, who must apply separately.
question: A Canadian Armed Forces member moves to Saskatchewan with a spouse and dependent children. Why should the family not assume everyone receives health coverage through the same program?
reference_answer: Canadian Armed Forces members receive health coverage through federal programs, while spouses and other eligible dependants ordinarily must apply for Saskatchewan's provincial health coverage. The family should check each person's eligibility and avoid assuming that federal coverage for the service member automatically includes dependants.

context_text: Saskatchewan student studying outside province needs to update contact/address and submit proof of full-time enrolment and return intent. If studying outside Canada, medical insurance beyond limited provincial out-of-country coverage is recommended.
question: Je suis titulaire d'une carte santé de la Saskatchewan et pars étudier à temps plein à l'extérieur de la province avant de revenir y vivre. Quelles démarches faut-il vérifier pour maintenir mon admissibilité?
reference_answer: Il faut aviser eHealth Saskatchewan de l'absence temporaire, mettre à jour ses coordonnées et fournir une preuve d'inscription à temps plein ainsi qu'une indication de l'intention de revenir vivre en Saskatchewan après les études. Une carte physique conservée ne prouve pas à elle seule que la couverture reste active. Si les études se déroulent hors du Canada, la province recommande aussi une assurance médicale additionnelle.

context_text: Saskatchewan says where spouse arrives within 12 months joint coverage starts first day third month after later arrival. If spouse arrives more than 12 months after first spouse the coverage dates are assessed independently.
question: I move to Saskatchewan before my spouse, who will join me later. Which facts are essential before predicting when our provincial health coverage will begin?
reference_answer: Ask when each spouse arrived or plans to arrive, whether both are eligible Saskatchewan residents, and whether the later-arriving spouse comes within twelve months of the first. eHealth Saskatchewan says that if a spouse joins within twelve months, coverage for both ordinarily begins the first day of the third month after that spouse arrives; if the gap exceeds twelve months, the coverage dates are determined separately. One person's arrival date is therefore insufficient.

context_text: A TFSA withdrawal restores contribution room beginning January 1 of the following calendar year. If no room remains, same-year recontribution of withdrawn funds can be an overcontribution.
question: I used all my TFSA contribution room and then withdrew $2,000 during the current calendar year. Can I automatically contribute that $2,000 back immediately, and when does the withdrawal become new room?
reference_answer: No, not when you have no other unused TFSA room. The withdrawn $2,000 is normally added to your available contribution room on January 1 of the following calendar year. Replacing it earlier without other available room may create an over-contribution subject to tax.

context_text: TFSA withdrawal doesn't add room until next January 1. With $1,000 unused room, a $3,000 current-year withdrawal leaves $1,000 available room for rest of year.
question: J'ai encore 1 000 $ de droits de cotisation inutilisés à mon CELI pour l'année en cours, puis je retire 3 000 $. Sans autre changement, combien puis-je cotiser au CELI au cours de cette même année sans dépasser mes droits?
reference_answer: 1 000 $. Le retrait de 3 000 $ ne crée pas immédiatement de nouveaux droits : il sera réintégré aux droits de cotisation le 1er janvier de l'année civile suivante. Le fait de le reverser la même année, au-delà des 1 000 $ de droits restants, créerait une cotisation excédentaire pouvant entraîner un impôt mensuel.

context_text: CRA displayed TFSA contribution room reflects prior-year reporting and updates annually rather than immediately. CRA recommends account-holder track own records from all TFSA issuers to avoid overcontributions. CRA contribution room is not real time and account history must be checked with institutions. A TFSA withdrawal during a calendar year increases available room in the following calendar year.
question: My CRA account's displayed TFSA contribution room does not yet reflect a recent withdrawal. Which records should I use to avoid making an excess contribution?
reference_answer: Calculate your own TFSA contribution room using statements from every TFSA provider, all contributions and withdrawals, and the annual room rules. The CRA account figure is not a real-time ledger: providers generally report prior-year TFSA transactions after year-end, and the CRA updates the displayed information later. A withdrawal made during the current year adds room only on January 1 of the following year, so do not treat it as immediately available to recontribute.

context_text: Canadian income-tax residency is determined through relevant residential ties and circumstances. Grant of permanent-resident immigration status alone does not determine tax-residency start.
question: I just received Canadian permanent-resident status. Is the issue date on that immigration document automatically my Canadian income-tax residency start date? What else matters?
reference_answer: No. Immigration status and income-tax residency are assessed under different rules. The CRA considers the relevant facts, including when significant residential ties were established, the purpose and continuity of the stay, and any applicable tax treaty. The PR document date alone is insufficient to determine a tax-residency start date.

context_text: Canada's main credit bureaus Equifax and TransUnion provide free credit reports. Checking your own credit report or credit score does not affect your credit score.
question: I need my Canadian credit history before renting. Which two main credit bureaus provide free reports, and will checking my own report lower my credit score?
reference_answer: Equifax and TransUnion are Canada's two main credit bureaus. Both offer free credit reports. Checking your own report or score is a soft inquiry and does not lower your credit score.

context_text: Bank tax withholding is applied to ordinary RRSP withdrawal. The withdrawal must be reported on income tax return and withholding may be insufficient for final tax due.
question: My Canadian bank withheld income tax from an ordinary RRSP withdrawal. Is that withholding necessarily the final tax I will owe on the withdrawal?
reference_answer: No. An ordinary taxable RRSP withdrawal must be included on the income tax return, and the tax withheld by the financial institution is credited toward the final tax liability. Depending on total taxable income, residence and tax bracket, you may owe more tax or have excess withholding refunded. Québec withdrawals can have separate federal and provincial withholding components; withholding is not a final tax determination.

context_text: CRA lists lower Quebec federal RRSP withholding percentages plus additional provincial withholding. A Quebec RRSP withdrawal of up to $5,000 has 5% federal withholding rather than 10% elsewhere, and a separate Quebec provincial withholding; withholding may differ from final tax.
question: Je compare les retenues sur un retrait de REER pour un résident du Québec et un résident d'une autre province. Pourquoi le taux de retenue fédérale réduit indiqué pour le Québec ne représente-t-il pas toute la retenue?
reference_answer: Parce que des retenues d'impôt provincial québécois s'ajoutent à la retenue fédérale. L'Agence du revenu du Canada indique par exemple un taux fédéral de 5 % au Québec, contre 10 % ailleurs, pour un retrait d'au plus 5 000 $, mais cela ne signifie ni que la retenue totale au Québec est de 5 % ni que la retenue égale l'impôt final à payer.

context_text: Basic CESG is generally 20% of qualifying RESP contribution up to per-year and lifetime limits. $2000 eligible RESP contribution yields $400 basic CESG excluding income-based additions.
question: For a Canada Education Savings Grant–eligible RESP beneficiary with no use of carry-forward room, a family contributes $2,000 this calendar year. What basic CESG is generated under the 20% rule, excluding income-tested additions?
reference_answer: $400 in basic Canada Education Savings Grant, because 20% × $2,000 = $400. This assumes the beneficiary is eligible, the funds count as grant-eligible RESP contributions, and there is sufficient remaining annual and lifetime grant room. Any additional CESG based on adjusted family income is separate and not included in this amount.

context_text: CESG basic rate 20% applies across incomes, but extra amount depends on family net income. Catch-up unused grant room and beneficiary limits may change total grant payable.
question: Deux familles canadiennes versent le même montant dans des REEE distincts. Peut-on leur promettre le même montant total de Subvention canadienne pour l'épargne-études?
reference_answer: Non. La subvention de base suit normalement le même taux de 20 % pour les cotisations admissibles, mais la subvention supplémentaire peut dépendre du revenu familial net rajusté. Les droits inutilisés reportés, l'âge et l'admissibilité de chaque bénéficiaire et les plafonds annuels ou à vie peuvent aussi différer. Il faut vérifier ces éléments avant de chiffrer la subvention totale d'un REEE.

context_text: A Canadian RESP's educational assistance payments are income to student beneficiary. Withdrawal of original RESP contributions is not taxable and can be returned to subscriber.
question: Dans un régime enregistré d'épargne-études (REEE), un paiement d'aide aux études (PAE) et le remboursement des cotisations ont-ils le même traitement fiscal? À qui le PAE est-il attribué?
reference_answer: Non. Le PAE comprend notamment les subventions, bons et revenus accumulés du REEE; il est versé au bénéficiaire étudiant et est généralement inclus dans son revenu imposable pour l'année de réception. Le retrait des cotisations initiales n'est pas imposable : le souscripteur peut les retirer sans impôt et choisir de les remettre au bénéficiaire.

context_text: RESP educational assistance payments may be used for rent, books, tools, transport as well as tuition. The subscriber requests EAP from promoter with enrolment proof and benefit is generally taxable income of beneficiary.
question: A student wants an RESP educational assistance payment to help cover rent and tools as well as tuition. Can the money be used for those costs, and who requests the payment?
reference_answer: Yes. Eligible RESP educational assistance payments (EAPs) can pay education-related expenses including tuition, books, tools, rent and transportation, not tuition alone. The plan's subscriber asks its RESP promoter for the EAP, and the promoter checks proof that the beneficiary is enrolled in an eligible full- or part-time post-secondary program. The EAP is generally taxable income to the beneficiary.

context_text: Retraite Québec includes CPP contributions in QPP pension calculation and may coordinate payment with CPP.
question: J'ai cotisé au Régime de rentes du Québec (RRQ), puis au Régime de pensions du Canada (RPC) ailleurs au pays. Est-il exact que mes cotisations au RPC sont automatiquement perdues pour le calcul de ma retraite?
reference_answer: Non. Retraite Québec prend en compte les cotisations au RPC dans le calcul des droits à la rente du RRQ. La démarche pour demander une rente et l'organisme qui la verse peuvent dépendre de l'endroit où vous résidez et de vos cotisations. Il faut vérifier le relevé de participation aux deux régimes plutôt que supposer des années perdues.

context_text: Applying for QPP pension before 65 permanently reduces monthly pension amount. At 60 it is approximately 30–36% lower than beginning at 65 under published 2026 pension schedules.
question: Une personne admissible au Régime de rentes du Québec envisage de commencer sa rente de retraite à 60 ans plutôt qu'à 65 ans. Quelle conséquence durable doit-elle comprendre?
reference_answer: Le fait de commencer la rente du RRQ avant 65 ans réduit normalement son montant chaque mois pour le reste de la vie. Selon Retraite Québec, le début à 60 ans produit une réduction d'environ 30 % à 36 % comparativement à 65 ans, selon la situation. Les besoins immédiats, la santé, l'emploi et les autres sources de revenu peuvent influencer le choix, mais la réduction de départ est durable.

context_text: An Interac Request Money notification asks recipient to send payment, not evidence of money received.
question: A buyer who claims to have paid you sends an Interac e-Transfer 'Request Money' notification. Should you accept that request as proof that you received payment?
reference_answer: No. A Request Money notification asks its recipient to send money to the requester; it is not proof of payment to you. Do not fulfill a request merely because the buyer says it is payment. Check the direction and status of the transaction in your own banking app, and independently confirm any unexpected notification.

context_text: Interac Autodeposit deposits funds automatically without security question if recipient is enrolled.
question: Mon colocataire au Canada me propose un virement Interac avec dépôt automatique. Quelle différence ce mode de réception présente-t-il par rapport à un dépôt qui exige une question de sécurité?
reference_answer: Si le dépôt automatique a été activé auprès de l'institution financière pour l'adresse courriel ou le numéro de téléphone associé, les fonds reçus sont normalement déposés directement dans le compte choisi, sans devoir répondre à une question de sécurité. Il faut vérifier le réglage auprès de sa banque ou caisse et confirmer les fonds dans le compte, plutôt que se fier seulement à une notification.

context_text: Interac allows user to verify Autodeposit recipient's displayed legal name before a payment. Recipient name mismatch warrants independent verification before sending.
question: Before confirming an Interac e-Transfer to someone using Autodeposit, the recipient name shown differs from the person you intended to pay. What should you do?
reference_answer: Pause rather than sending. Interac displays the registered recipient's name for many Autodeposit transfers before confirmation; compare it with the intended payee and independently verify the correct address or phone number and identity. An unexpected name is a reason to stop and investigate, not a minor detail to ignore. Contact the financial institution if you suspect fraud or have already transferred the funds.

context_text: Interac does not request bank passwords via email or SMS. Suspicious notifications should be verified via independent bank channel, not emailed link.
question: Un courriel prétend venir d'Interac et exige mon mot de passe bancaire pour débloquer un virement. Quelle réponse est fiable?
reference_answer: Ne donnez jamais ce mot de passe et n'utilisez pas les liens du message. Interac affirme ne jamais demander un mot de passe bancaire par courriel ou par texto. Vérifiez toute opération directement dans votre application bancaire ou auprès de votre institution financière en utilisant des coordonnées indépendantes. Vous pouvez transmettre le message suspect à phishing@interac.ca.

context_text: Canadian direct deposit banking coordinates use institution, transit and account numbers. An e-Transfer email is not sufficient to provide payroll direct-deposit details.
question: A Canadian payroll direct-deposit form asks for account, institution and transit numbers. What banking information should I find instead of entering the email address I use for Interac e-Transfers?
reference_answer: Retrieve the direct-deposit details for the account where you want to receive pay: your account number, the financial institution number and the branch/transit number. Banks typically show these in account details or on a downloadable void cheque or direct-deposit form. An Interac e-Transfer email address identifies a different payment route and does not replace these banking numbers.

context_text: Basic groceries such as milk, bread and vegetables are GST/HST zero-rated at 0%. The same store can sell other normally taxable items at nonzero GST/HST rates.
question: A Canadian grocery receipt shows 0% GST/HST on ordinary milk, bread and vegetables. Does that mean this store has stopped charging GST/HST on all products?
reference_answer: No. In Canada, basic grocery supplies such as ordinary milk, bread and vegetables are usually zero-rated, meaning GST/HST applies at 0%. Other supplies such as candy, carbonated beverages or non-food products may be taxed at the appropriate provincial or territorial GST/HST rate. Zero-rating is a property of the supply, not evidence of a store-wide tax exemption.

context_text: CRA defines zero-rated GST/HST taxable supplies at 0% and exempt supplies differently, including input tax credits. CRA permits relevant input tax credits on zero-rated taxable supplies but generally not on exempt supplies even though neither carries consumer GST/HST.
question: In a Canadian tax explanation for a registered business, are GST/HST 'zero-rated' supplies and 'exempt' supplies interchangeable simply because customers pay no GST/HST on either?
reference_answer: No. A zero-rated supply is taxable at a 0% GST/HST rate, and related input tax credits may be available. An exempt supply is outside GST/HST charging and generally does not permit input tax credits on the related purchases. Both can result in no GST/HST charged to the customer, but their legal and accounting treatments differ.

context_text: GST/HST rate depends on classification of supply and legally determined place of supply. Rates for ordinary taxable supplies differ across provinces and territories while zero-rated supplies are 0%.
question: Une entreprise canadienne veut connaître le taux de TPS/TVH à facturer, mais ne précise ni le bien ou service vendu ni le lieu de fourniture. Quelles informations faut-il obtenir avant de répondre?
reference_answer: Il faut identifier la nature de la fourniture, pour savoir si elle est taxable au taux normal, détaxée à 0 % ou exonérée, ainsi que son lieu de fourniture selon les règles de l'ARC. Les taux de TPS/TVH varient entre provinces et territoires pour les fournitures taxables ordinaires; une entreprise « canadienne » n'a pas un seul taux universel. L'adresse du client ne détermine pas forcément à elle seule le lieu de fourniture.

context_text: Quebec National Day is June 24, whereas Canada Day is July 1. Both are holiday dates in Quebec but June 24 has different legal compensation conditions. The June 24 Québec Fête nationale celebrates Québec's culture and identity; July 1 Canada Day historically celebrates the July 1867 Confederation anniversary. Two official independent celebration pages support the cultural/historical distinction omitted from CNESST's employment holiday listing.
question: Je prépare un calendrier de travail au Québec. Comment distinguer la fête nationale du Québec de la fête du Canada, sans les présenter comme une seule et même célébration?
reference_answer: La fête nationale du Québec est le 24 juin et célèbre l'identité et les traditions québécoises; elle est régie par des dispositions particulières de la Loi sur la fête nationale. La fête du Canada a lieu le 1er juillet et commémore la Confédération, avec des règles de jour férié distinctes. Toutes deux figurent parmi les jours fériés québécois, mais leur origine, leur signification et certaines modalités de congé ne sont pas les mêmes.

context_text: Quebec worker on ordinary statutory holiday must be paid for work performed. Employer also owes statutory indemnity or compensatory paid leave.
question: Une salariée qui relève des normes du travail du Québec est tenue de travailler lors d'un jour férié ordinaire. Est-ce que l'employeur n'a qu'à lui payer ses heures habituelles?
reference_answer: Non. L'employeur doit payer le salaire des heures travaillées et, en compensation du jour férié normalement chômé, choisir entre verser une indemnité supplémentaire calculée selon les règles de la CNESST ou accorder un congé compensatoire payé. Le congé d'un jour férié ordinaire est généralement accordé dans les trois semaines précédant ou suivant la date. Pour le 24 juin, fête nationale, certaines modalités particulières s'appliquent.

context_text: Alberta Heritage Day and Boxing Day are optional general holidays, not mandatory under provincial standards. Employer can choose to recognize an optional holiday and then applicable holiday-pay rules apply.
question: My Alberta workplace calendar lists Heritage Day and Boxing Day. Before assuming they are mandatory paid statutory holidays under provincial employment standards, what should I verify?
reference_answer: Both Heritage Day and Boxing Day are listed as optional general holidays in Alberta's employment standards. Ask whether your employer has chosen to recognize them or whether your employment contract or collective agreement provides them. Also check whether you work in a federally regulated industry, where different holiday rules may apply. A calendar listing alone does not establish a statutory Alberta paid-holiday entitlement.

context_text: Alberta local retail workplaces generally fall under provincial employment standards. Federally regulated employers such as banks are subject to distinct federal labour standards.
question: Two people work in Calgary, one at a local retail store and another in an industry under federal labour jurisdiction. Why might different statutory-holiday rules apply even though they work in the same city?
reference_answer: Employment standards follow jurisdiction, not simply the city's location. An ordinary local Alberta retail workplace generally falls under Alberta's Employment Standards Code and its general-holiday rules, whereas a federally regulated workplace—such as a bank or interprovincial transport business—falls under the Canada Labour Code and federal holiday provisions. Their paid-holiday entitlements and exceptions may therefore differ; check the actual employer and job.

context_text: Quebec price accuracy policy compensation for eligible goods advertised over $15 is $15 off displayed price. For displayed $28 scanned $31, corrected total is $13 before tax. A pricing error for an eligible product advertised above $15 yields $15 discount from corrected advertised price. A $28 advertised eligible product scanned at $31 costs $13 before tax, with tax on actual amount.
question: Dans un commerce québécois assujetti à la Politique d'exactitude des prix, un article admissible annoncé à 28 $ est facturé 31 $ à la caisse. Quel prix avant taxes doit-on normalement payer après le dédommagement de 2026?
reference_answer: 13 $ avant taxes. Comme le prix annoncé est supérieur à 15 $, le commerçant doit corriger le prix de 31 $ à 28 $, puis appliquer un rabais de 15 $ sur le prix annoncé : 28 $ − 15 $ = 13 $. Les taxes sont calculées sur les 13 $ payés, sous réserve des exceptions à la Politique, par exemple certains articles exclus.

context_text: Quebec policy requires correction for each identical item with erroneous scanned price. Free item or $15 reduction compensation applies to only one identical item per repeated error.
question: Trois articles identiques sont chacun facturés trop cher dans un commerce québécois assujetti à la Politique d'exactitude des prix. Le dédommagement s'applique-t-il séparément à chacun?
reference_answer: Non. Le commerçant doit corriger le prix de chacun des trois articles au plus bas prix annoncé applicable. Toutefois, si les articles sont identiques et présentent la même erreur, le dédommagement (gratuité pour un article de 15 $ ou moins ou rabais de 15 $ pour un article plus cher) s'applique une seule fois à un seul article. Les deux autres restent facturés au prix annoncé corrigé.

context_text: Individual article price labels ordinarily make Quebec scan-price compensation policy inapplicable. Retailer still must honour lowest advertised/labelled price rather than higher scanned price.
question: Au Québec, un commerçant étiquette individuellement le prix sur chaque article, mais la caisse affiche un montant supérieur à l'étiquette. Peut-on exiger automatiquement le dédommagement de 15 $?
reference_answer: Non. Un commerce qui affiche les prix individuellement sur chaque article n'est pas, de ce seul fait, assujetti à la Politique d'exactitude des prix prévoyant la gratuité ou le rabais de 15 $. Il doit toutefois vendre l'article au prix annoncé, jamais à un prix supérieur; si plusieurs prix sont affichés, le plus bas peut s'appliquer selon les règles. Vérifiez si le commerçant utilise réellement l'exemption d'étiquetage individuel avant de réclamer la compensation.

context_text: DEP means diplôme d'études professionnelles in Quebec. Credential signifies vocational education for trade/occupation and not a university degree.
question: Dans une offre d'emploi au Québec, on exige un « DEP ». De quel diplôme et de quel type de formation québécoise s'agit-il?
reference_answer: DEP signifie « diplôme d'études professionnelles ». Dans le système scolaire québécois, il est obtenu après une formation professionnelle visant l'exercice d'un métier spécialisé, généralement rattachée à l'enseignement secondaire. Il ne s'agit ni d'un diplôme collégial de type DEC ni d'un diplôme universitaire.

context_text: Quebec publicly funded preschool, primary and secondary education normally taught in French. English instruction eligibility requires satisfying Charter of French Language exceptions.
question: Une famille récemment arrivée au Québec souhaite inscrire ses enfants à une école publique de langue anglaise. Quelle condition faut-il examiner avant d'affirmer que ce choix est possible?
reference_answer: Il faut vérifier l'admissibilité des enfants à l'enseignement en anglais selon la Charte de la langue française et les règles administratives. Le français est normalement la langue d'enseignement du préscolaire, du primaire et du secondaire. Des critères d'exception existent, notamment liés à la citoyenneté et au parcours scolaire des parents ou des frères et sœurs, et certaines autorisations temporaires. Une simple préférence familiale ne garantit pas l'inscription dans le réseau public anglophone.

context_text: BC Class 7 N novice driver generally only permitted one passenger absent family/supervisor exception. 22-year-old with 3 unrelated friends and no supervisor does not qualify under 2026 ICBC rules. ICBC notes October 19 2026 change in supervisor age; the no-supervisor three-friends scenario remains prohibited.
question: A 22-year-old driver in British Columbia holds a Class 7 'N' licence and offers to drive three unrelated friends to an event, without a qualified supervisor. Is that within the current novice passenger restrictions?
reference_answer: No. ICBC's current Class 7 novice rules generally allow only one passenger unless all additional passengers are immediate family members or a qualifying supervisor accompanies the driver. Three unrelated friends without such supervision do not qualify. The driver's age of 22 does not remove the passenger restriction. Note that the qualification age for some supervisors changed on October 19, 2026, so current ICBC rules should be used.

context_text: Canadian child car seat needs Transport Canada National Safety Mark, including imported seats. Local legal rules vary with child's age, height, weight and seating requirements.
question: A newcomer wants to buy a cheaper child car seat outside Canada for use in Canada. What Canadian requirements should they verify before purchasing?
reference_answer: Confirm that the seat has Canada's National Safety Mark and required Canadian product information label, indicating compliance with Canadian restraint standards. Foreign certification alone, including a U.S. approval, does not establish Canadian certification. Also check the provincial or territorial rules for the child's age, height and weight, the seat's manufacturer's limits, vehicle fit and installation instructions. Do not assume an overseas seat without the National Safety Mark is legal for use in Canada.

context_text: Provincial and territorial rules for booster seats vary and depend on child characteristics. Lawful and safe booster discontinuation depends on belt fit and child's size/age; scenario lacks essential details.
question: Mon enfant peut-il cesser d'utiliser son siège d'appoint? Je n'ai pas précisé la province ou le territoire, l'âge, le poids ni la taille de mon enfant. Quelles données faut-il demander?
reference_answer: Demandez la province ou le territoire de circulation, l'âge, la taille et le poids de l'enfant, puis vérifiez les limites du siège et si la ceinture du véhicule s'ajuste correctement à son corps. Transports Canada rappelle que les exigences légales d'utilisation diffèrent d'une province ou d'un territoire à l'autre. Sans ces informations, il serait imprudent de déclarer le siège d'appoint inutile.

context_text: CFL has 12 players per team, three downs and 65-yard-wide field. NFL contrasting rules use 11 players, four downs and narrower field.
question: At my first Canadian Football League game, what differences from NFL football should I expect in the number of downs, players per side and field width?
reference_answer: In the CFL, the offence normally has three downs to make ten yards, there are 12 players per team on the field, and the field is 65 yards wide. The NFL uses four downs, 11 players and a field approximately 53⅓ yards wide. The CFL also permits characteristic backfield motion before the snap, often called the 'waggle'.

context_text: CFL rulebook defines continuous backfield motion as waggle. Waggle is an allowed Canadian football pre-snap movement, not literal shaking.
question: Dans un commentaire sur un match de la Ligue canadienne de football, que signifie « waggle »? Expliquez le terme en français courant, sans le traduire mot à mot.
reference_answer: Le « waggle » est le mouvement continu de joueurs offensifs du champ arrière avant la remise en jeu au football canadien. Les receveurs et certains autres joueurs peuvent prendre de l'élan vers la ligne de mêlée avant la remise, selon les règles de la LCF. Il ne s'agit pas simplement d'une gesticulation ni d'une pénalité; c'est une particularité du jeu canadien.

context_text: Quebec couples may designate a close relative as a one-day legally authorized officiant. The Directeur de l'état civil must authorize the designated celebrant for specific ceremony.
question: Nous aimerions que ma sœur célèbre légalement notre mariage civil au Québec. Quelle démarche faut-il faire avant de lui confier la cérémonie?
reference_answer: Votre sœur doit obtenir du Directeur de l'état civil une désignation particulière comme célébrante d'un jour, valable pour votre mariage à la date prévue. Elle et les futurs époux doivent présenter la demande avec les renseignements requis. La désignation exige notamment d'avoir au moins 18 ans, d'être citoyenne canadienne ou de résider au Québec et de respecter les conditions de célébration. Le simple fait d'être une proche ou de diriger la cérémonie symbolique ne remplace pas cette autorisation.

context_text: Quebec notaries authorized to receive notarial acts can solemnize civil marriages. Directeur de l'état civil maintains registry of legally authorized celebrants.
question: We want a civil wedding in Quebec. May a notary officiate, and where can we check that the person is authorized?
reference_answer: Yes. Notaries authorized to receive notarial acts are among the people permitted by Quebec law to solemnize a civil marriage. The Directeur de l'état civil maintains a register of authorized marriage and civil-union officiants, including notaries. Verify the individual in that register and confirm they are available and will meet the legal notice and ceremony requirements.

context_text: Newfoundland not included in Canada's 1931 census because it joined Confederation in 1949. Separate Newfoundland census returns exist for 1921,1935,1945.
question: I am researching relatives who lived in Newfoundland in 1931. Why might Canada's national 1931 Census fail to include them, and what alternative historical collections should I search?
reference_answer: Newfoundland did not join Confederation until 1949, so the Canadian 1931 national census did not cover Newfoundland. Search separate Newfoundland census records, especially the 1921, 1935 and 1945 Newfoundland censuses, plus local records. Library and Archives Canada has access aids and microfilm listings; the Provincial Archives of Newfoundland and Labrador at The Rooms holds original returns. Labrador has some exceptional historical entries in other Canadian census collections, so check the exact location.

context_text: Individual Canadian census returns remain confidential until statutory 92-year access period. Published 2021 aggregate tables do not make identifiable responses public.
question: Les statistiques du Recensement de 2021 sont publiées. Puis-je donc consulter librement la fiche nominative de ma grand-mère dans ce recensement?
reference_answer: Non. Les tableaux statistiques diffusés par Statistique Canada sont agrégés et ne rendent pas publiques les réponses personnelles identifiables du Recensement de 2021. En vertu des règles applicables aux dossiers historiques, les déclarations individuelles sont normalement transférées à Bibliothèque et Archives Canada et ouvertes au public après 92 ans. Il ne faut donc pas confondre la publication de statistiques 2021 avec l'accès aux fiches nominatives de 2021.

context_text: LAC says questions and completeness vary between census years. Blank census fields are not evidence of unemployment without checking questionnaire and source.
question: My genealogy spreadsheet shows a blank occupation field for an ancestor in a Canadian historical census. Can I conclude they were unemployed?
reference_answer: No. A blank could mean the occupation question did not apply, was asked differently in that year, was left unanswered, was recorded on a damaged or incomplete return, or was missed during transcription. Library and Archives Canada warns that census questionnaires and completeness vary over time. Examine that census year's form, instructions and original image before inferring employment status; a blank alone is not proof of unemployment.

context_text: November 11 is Remembrance Day. Two-minute silence at 11 a.m. is customary Canadian remembrance activity.
question: Rédigez une phrase naturelle pour une annonce canadienne en français invitant le public à observer deux minutes de silence le 11 novembre à 11 h.
reference_answer: À l'occasion du jour du Souvenir, nous vous invitons à observer deux minutes de silence le 11 novembre à 11 h, en mémoire des personnes qui ont servi et de celles qui ont perdu la vie.

context_text: Canadian Labour Day occurs first Monday September. France Labour Day is May 1; Canadian French capitalization variants exist.
question: Je traduis pour un calendrier canadien « Labour Day: first Monday in September ». Quelle formulation évite de confondre cette fête avec le 1er mai célébré en France?
reference_answer: « Fête du Travail : premier lundi de septembre. » Au Canada, la fête du Travail a lieu le premier lundi de septembre. En France, la fête du Travail est associée au 1er mai; le même nom ne désigne donc pas la même date. La graphie « fête du travail » est aussi admise selon le Portail linguistique du Canada.

context_text: Quebec Journée nationale des patriotes established 2002, commemorates 1837–1838 Patriotes. Victoria Day commemorates Queen Victoria and falls same Monday before May 25.
question: Why does a Quebec calendar call the May Monday holiday Journée nationale des patriotes while a calendar elsewhere in Canada calls that date Victoria Day?
reference_answer: The two holidays fall on the Monday preceding May 25, but commemorate different events. Quebec's Journée nationale des patriotes, established in 2002, honours the Patriotes' 1837–1838 struggle for political liberty and democratic government in Lower Canada. Victoria Day, observed in much of the rest of Canada, commemorates Queen Victoria's birthday and the monarchy. Treat them as jurisdiction-specific names with distinct historical meanings, not as interchangeable cultural labels.

context_text: Foreign credential licensing depends on regulated occupation. Canadian provincial or territorial regulator requirements differ by jurisdiction and profession.
question: I trained abroad and want to enter a regulated profession in Canada. Before recommending a licensing process, what information should an assistant confirm?
reference_answer: Confirm that the intended country is Canada, then ask which specific occupation or profession the person plans to practise and in which province or territory. Licensing and foreign-credential recognition are handled by profession-specific provincial or territorial regulators in many fields, not by a single universal federal licensing office. The regulator can explain required credential assessment, supervised practice, examinations and other steps.

context_text: Explore funding requires Canadian citizenship or permanent residence. International student on study permit alone is ineligible for federally funded Explore place.
question: I am studying in Canada on a temporary study permit and want a Government of Canada-funded Explore language-immersion place. What eligibility condition should I check before applying?
reference_answer: Explore funding requires Canadian citizenship or permanent resident status, as well as the age and student-status criteria. Being an international student in Canada on a study permit alone does not meet the citizenship or permanent residence requirement. An international student could ask the institution about paying personally for an unfunded place, but should not assume eligibility for the funded subsidy.

context_text: 2021 Indigenous average age was 33.6 years.
question: Pour planifier des services à la jeunesse autochtone, quelles différences d'âge moyen le Recensement de 2021 révèle-t-il entre les populations autochtone et non autochtone? Quelle prudence faut-il garder?
reference_answer: Au Recensement de 2021, la moyenne d'âge était de 33,6 ans dans la population autochtone et de 41,8 ans dans la population non autochtone, soit un écart moyen de 8,2 ans. Cette différence peut justifier d'examiner attentivement les services destinés aux jeunes, mais elle ne décrit pas chaque Nation, chaque communauté ou chaque personne. Les besoins doivent être déterminés avec les communautés et des données locales.

context_text: 2021 Western Canada together had 55.5% of First Nations population. Ontario single province had largest total, 251030 persons representing 23.9%.
question: In Canada's 2021 Census, over half of First Nations people lived in Western Canada, yet Ontario had the largest provincial count. How can both findings be true?
reference_answer: Western Canada groups together several provinces, while Ontario is a single province. Across western provinces collectively, 55.5% of the First Nations population lived there in 2021. Ontario alone had 251,030 First Nations residents, 23.9% of Canada's First Nations population—more than any other individual province. A multi-province region can exceed half of a national total while a province outside it has the largest individual provincial count.

context_text: 2021 Indigenous persons living in CMAs 801045. 2016 to 2021 Indigenous CMA population increased 12.5%; CMA excludes smaller agglomerations.
question: Au Recensement de 2021, environ combien de personnes autochtones vivaient dans les grands centres urbains canadiens, et comment ce nombre avait-il évolué depuis 2016?
reference_answer: En 2021, 801 045 personnes autochtones vivaient dans les grands centres urbains, définis ici comme les régions métropolitaines de recensement (RMR) d'au moins 100 000 habitants. Leur nombre avait augmenté de 12,5 % depuis 2016. Attention : ce chiffre ne représente pas l'ensemble des zones urbaines; si on y ajoute les agglomérations de recensement plus petites, le total est plus élevé.

context_text: Ontario had more than half of French-only first-official-language speakers outside Quebec in 2021. 2021 province percentages French-only FOLS Ontario 3.4%, New Brunswick 30.0%.
question: Pour joindre les communautés francophones hors Québec, pourquoi faut-il distinguer le nombre de personnes de leur proportion dans chaque province? Comparez l'Ontario et le Nouveau-Brunswick selon la première langue officielle parlée au Recensement de 2021.
reference_answer: L'Ontario regroupait plus de la moitié des francophones hors Québec dont le français était la seule première langue officielle parlée, mais ceux-ci ne représentaient que 3,4 % de sa population provinciale. Au Nouveau-Brunswick, leur nombre absolu était plus faible, mais leur poids dans la population était de 30,0 %. La taille d'une communauté à joindre et sa proportion régionale sont deux indicateurs distincts; il faut choisir les deux selon le service à planifier.

context_text: Country food access is central to Inuit food security and cultural practices. ITK prioritizes harvesting and sharing, food sovereignty, infrastructure and Inuit-led solutions.
question: Why would an Inuit-led food-security initiative in Inuit Nunangat support harvesting and sharing country foods as well as improving access to store-bought groceries?
reference_answer: Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami describes country foods gathered through hunting, fishing and other harvesting as central to Inuit diet, cultural continuity, skills and kinship. Food security therefore means access to safe, nutritious, culturally preferred foods—not just more items on store shelves. Supporting equipment, local harvesting, processing, storage and sharing systems can strengthen food sovereignty and livelihoods alongside measures addressing high retail prices.

context_text: ITK food research and evaluation should be based on Inuit priorities and leadership. Inuit food self-determination includes wildlife management and country-food harvesting.
question: Une équipe externe mène une étude sur la sécurité alimentaire dans l'Inuit Nunangat. Comment devrait-elle définir les questions et les méthodes de recherche selon les priorités d'Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami?
reference_answer: Elle doit travailler avec les instances inuites et sous leur leadership pour que les questions, méthodes et usages des résultats répondent aux priorités inuites. La Stratégie de sécurité alimentaire de l'Inuit Nunangat demande que la recherche et l'évaluation reposent sur l'autodétermination et prennent en compte la souveraineté alimentaire, les systèmes de récolte et de partage ainsi que les décisions inuites en matière de gestion faunique. Elle ne devrait pas imposer un modèle strictement méridional de disponibilité d'épicerie.

context_text: Fishing Lake Métis Settlement interprets infinity symbol as unity of cultures. Infinity on Métis flag represents continuity of Métis traditions and values. It additionally signifies the continuity of Métis culture, values, traditions and people across time.
question: Dans une présentation sur le drapeau métis, comment expliquer le symbole blanc en forme de huit couché, sans le réduire à un motif décoratif?
reference_answer: Le symbole de l'infini blanc du drapeau métis représente, selon le Fishing Lake Métis Settlement, l'union de deux traditions culturelles et la continuité du peuple métis, de ses valeurs et de sa culture à travers les générations. Il exprime une identité collective durable, et non simplement une décoration graphique. Les interprétations peuvent être enrichies par les connaissances des communautés et des autorités métisses concernées.

context_text: 2021 national seniors 65+ share about 19%. 2021 proportion seniors Newfoundland Labrador ~24% vs Nunavut ~4%.
question: Why would using Canada's overall 2021 percentage of seniors for both Newfoundland and Labrador and Nunavut be a poor starting point for local service planning?
reference_answer: The 2021 Census showed about 19% of Canadians were aged 65 or older, but Newfoundland and Labrador's proportion was roughly 24%, while Nunavut's was only about 4%. Applying the national average to both places would overstate seniors' share in Nunavut and understate it in Newfoundland and Labrador. Local population counts, geography and service needs must be assessed before allocating programs.

context_text: About 23000 Japanese Canadians were forcibly uprooted in 1942 and dispersed to varied restrictive settings. Their property was seized and sold with little compensation, a separate dispossession harm.
question: Why is the wartime treatment of Japanese Canadians in Canada described as both internment and dispossession?
reference_answer: Beginning in 1942, the Canadian government forcibly uprooted about 23,000 people of Japanese ancestry from coastal British Columbia, placing many in internment or detention camps and sending others to labour sites. It also seized and sold their homes, fishing boats, businesses and other property, often without adequate compensation. Internment describes restrictions on liberty and forced removal; dispossession describes the separate loss of property and economic security.

context_text: Japanese Canadian travel/property restrictions persisted after 1945, including deportation to Japan. Free movement across Canada was restored April 1 1949.
question: Une chronologie familiale canadienne indique que les restrictions imposées aux Canadiens japonais ont toutes pris fin avec la Seconde Guerre mondiale en 1945. Pourquoi serait-ce trompeur?
reference_answer: La fin de la guerre en 1945 n'a pas immédiatement mis fin aux restrictions. Les Canadiens japonais ont notamment été empêchés de retourner librement sur la côte de la Colombie-Britannique après le conflit, et environ 4 000 personnes ont été exilées au Japon. La liberté de circuler et de s'établir à nouveau partout au Canada n'a été rétablie que le 1er avril 1949.

context_text: 1988 redress agreement included apology, individual compensation and community fund. It also included pardons, citizenship remedies, and Race Relations Foundation support.
question: Why did the 1988 Japanese Canadian Redress Agreement involve more than a symbolic federal apology?
reference_answer: Alongside the September 22, 1988 apology, the agreement provided $21,000 individual compensation to eligible people directly affected, a community fund, pardons for those wrongfully imprisoned, citizenship remedies for some people exiled to Japan and their descendants, and $24 million toward what became the Canadian Race Relations Foundation. It recognized material and legal harms as well as emotional and historical injustice.

context_text: UVic Landscapes of Injustice prefers forced uprooting instead of evacuation. UVic Landscapes of Injustice prefers exile rather than repatriation for Japanese Canadians removed to Japan.
question: A Canadian museum text calls the forced removal of Japanese Canadians during the Second World War an 'evacuation' and their coerced departure to Japan a 'repatriation'. What historically more accurate wording should a curator use?
reference_answer: Describe the removal from communities as **forced uprooting** or **forced displacement**, and the government's removal of people to Japan as **exile**. For the overall wartime period, 'internment' or 'internment era' may also be appropriate depending on the context. These words reflect coercion rather than implying that people travelled voluntarily or were removed for their own protection; 'repatriation' is misleading for Canadian-born people.

context_text: Chinese workers helped construct CPR between 1880 and 1885. Canada enacted discriminatory Chinese head tax in 1885 after railway completion. The 1885 Chinese Immigration Act imposed an initial $50 head tax after Chinese labourers' contributions to railway construction, increased in 1900 and 1903. Canadian Heritage's Asian Heritage Month chronology directly establishes the $50 initial 1885 charge, which MHSO page had not numerically substantiated.
question: Quel paradoxe historique faut-il expliquer entre la contribution des travailleurs chinois à la construction du chemin de fer transcontinental et les restrictions d'immigration qui ont suivi?
reference_answer: Des milliers de travailleurs chinois ont joué un rôle essentiel dans la construction du chemin de fer du Canadien Pacifique, notamment de 1880 à 1885. Après l'achèvement du chemin de fer, le gouvernement fédéral a adopté en 1885 une taxe d'entrée de 50 $ visant expressément les immigrants chinois et destinée à limiter leur immigration. La taxe fut ensuite augmentée. Ce contraste montre la contribution indispensable de ces travailleurs et le racisme institutionnalisé qui a marqué les politiques migratoires du pays.

context_text: Government confiscated Kwakwaka'wakw ceremonial items after 1921 potlatch prosecutions. Communities secured partial repatriation to U'mista and other cultural centres after prolonged negotiations.
question: Pourquoi l'histoire de la collection du potlatch du Centre culturel U'mista relève-t-elle de la restitution plutôt que d'une simple acquisition muséale?
reference_answer: Dans les années 1920, des masques et objets cérémoniels kwakwaka'wakw ont été confisqués dans le cadre de la répression du potlatch, une cérémonie autochtone alors criminalisée par la Loi sur les Indiens. Ces objets ont été dispersés dans différents musées et collections privées, souvent sans consentement véritable. Les communautés et leurs descendants ont ensuite mené des démarches de plusieurs décennies pour obtenir leur retour. Le Centre culturel U'mista conserve et expose des objets restitués dans cette histoire de réappropriation culturelle.

context_text: U'mista states potlatch attendees witness cultural histories, naming, succession and other events. Witnesses receive gifts acknowledging that social function.
question: In the U'mista Cultural Centre's explanation of a Kwakwaka'wakw potlatch, why are invited people considered witnesses as well as guests?
reference_answer: A potlatch is a formal gathering in which families and communities publicly recount histories and mark events such as marriage, a naming, a new chief's succession or a death through song, dance and other practices. Invitees witness these declarations and help preserve communal knowledge of what took place. Gifts given to witnesses acknowledge that social and historical responsibility; the event is more than entertainment or hospitality.

context_text: Nisga'a pts'aan crests represent Adaawak oral histories and family/clan identities. Some poles document family lands or commemorate deceased Chiefs.
question: Comment présenter à des élèves la signification des emblèmes sur un pts'aan (mât sculpté) nisg̱a'a sans les réduire à des figures animales décoratives?
reference_answer: Selon les ressources linguistiques et culturelles nisg̱a'a, les emblèmes (ayukws) d'un pts'aan représentent des adaawaḵ, c'est-à-dire des récits oraux traditionnels, ainsi que des liens à des groupes de parenté et à l'histoire des familles, de leurs terres et de leurs ressources. Certains mâts servent à commémorer une personne décédée ou un chef. Leur interprétation précise dépend de la famille et de l'histoire propres au mât; on ne peut pas assigner une signification universelle à chaque animal.

context_text: Nisga'a crest pole symbols are tied to individual family oral histories. Universal animal code cannot determine exact provenance or narrative.
question: I have a photograph of a Nisg̱a'a crest pole and can see several carved animals, but I don't know its family or makers. Can you identify the pole's exact oral history from the animal list alone?
reference_answer: No, not reliably. A Nisg̱a'a pts'aan uses family-specific crests linked to adaawaḵ (oral histories), tribal and property relationships, and the purpose of the pole. The same animal category cannot be assigned a universal narrative independent of provenance. Ask the appropriate Nisg̱a'a family or cultural authority, or find a documented interpretation of this particular pole, rather than inventing a story.

context_text: Blackfoot Confederacy is four related nations including Southern Piikani in Montana. Blackfoot homelands extend across modern Alberta, Saskatchewan and Montana border.
question: Pourquoi une présentation de la Confédération des Pieds-Noirs ne doit-elle pas se limiter à la frontière actuelle entre le Canada et les États-Unis?
reference_answer: La Confédération des Pieds-Noirs (Siksikaitsitapi) réunit quatre nations apparentées : les Siksika, les Kainai et les Apatohsipiikani (Piikani du Nord) en Alberta, ainsi que les Aamsskáápipikani (Piikani du Sud, ou Blackfeet Nation) au Montana. Leur territoire traditionnel et leurs liens de parenté traversent la frontière internationale moderne. Il faut donc distinguer cette histoire et cette organisation transfrontalières des juridictions étatiques actuelles.

context_text: Canadian Language Portal prefers noun practice. Canadian Language Portal prefers verb and participle practise/practising.
