reference_answer: Les mandats spéciaux du gouverneur général peuvent autoriser temporairement certaines dépenses fédérales pendant la dissolution du Parlement, lorsqu'une dépense est jugée urgente pour l'intérêt public et qu'aucun crédit parlementaire n'est disponible. Leur utilisation est soumise à des conditions prévues dans la Loi sur la gestion des finances publiques, notamment une attestation du ministre concerné et du président du Conseil du Trésor. Ils ne servent pas à dépenser sans limite, ni pendant une simple prorogation.

context_text: Eligible BC riding voters can initiate recall of their elected MLA; approved petition organizers have 60 days to collect signatures. At least 40% of eligible original election voters must sign; if verified successful, MLA removed and by-election follows. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: Can voters in British Columbia seek to remove their MLA before the next election?
reference_answer: Yes. British Columbia has a statutory recall process under the Recall and Initiative Act. An eligible registered voter in the MLA's electoral district may apply to Elections BC for a recall petition. If approved, volunteers have 60 days to gather valid signatures from at least 40% of the voters eligible to sign it; if the threshold is met and verified, the MLA is removed and a by-election follows. Eligibility and timing requirements must be checked before initiating the petition.

context_text: Old Age Security recovery depends on annual net world income, not only Canadian-source earnings. For income year 2025 the published recovery threshold is $93,454; thresholds vary by tax year and repayment period. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: Pour l’impôt de récupération de la Sécurité de la vieillesse, le seuil dépend-il de mon revenu canadien seulement?
reference_answer: Non. L'impôt de récupération de la Sécurité de la vieillesse repose sur le revenu net mondial pour l'année d'imposition applicable, et non uniquement sur le revenu de source canadienne. Les revenus de sources étrangères sont donc pertinents. Si le revenu dépasse le seuil annuel, une partie ou la totalité de la pension peut être récupérée, selon la situation du bénéficiaire et les règles applicables. Pour 2025, le seuil de départ indiqué par Service Canada est de 93 454 $; ce seuil est indexé et change selon l'année.

context_text: Notice of assessment records CRA's initial income-tax return assessment; reassessment reflects a subsequent change. Reassessment can result from adjustment or review and does not alone prove fraud, additional tax or wrongdoing. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: Why did CRA send me a notice of reassessment instead of another notice of assessment?
reference_answer: A notice of assessment reports the CRA's initial assessment of your filed income-tax return. A notice of reassessment is issued if the CRA later changes that already-assessed return—for example after processing an adjustment request or revising an amount through a review. It summarizes the updated results, so receiving a reassessment does not by itself establish that you committed an offence or owe additional tax.

context_text: CRA requires taxpayers to wait for their original Notice of Assessment before requesting return changes. Existing modification requests should be processed before subsequent requests, with CRA online and paper mechanisms provided. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: Je viens d’envoyer ma déclaration fédérale et j’ai oublié un renseignement. Dois-je demander une modification tout de suite?
reference_answer: Non, pas immédiatement. Selon l'ARC, vous devez d'abord attendre l'avis de cotisation de la déclaration initiale avant de demander une modification. Une fois l'avis reçu, vous pouvez utiliser le service « Modifier ma déclaration » dans votre compte de l'ARC, ReTRANSMETTRE si vous êtes admissible, ou le formulaire de redressement prévu. Si vous avez déjà présenté une demande de modification, attendez la décision avant d'en soumettre une autre pour la même déclaration.

context_text: CRA email does not link to forms requesting personal or banking details for supposed tax refunds. Unsolicited refund phishing should not be followed; taxpayer should navigate official account or contact CRA independently. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: An email says CRA needs my bank details through a link to send my refund. Should I use it?
reference_answer: No. Do not follow an unsolicited email link or provide banking information to receive a supposed CRA refund. The CRA warns that its notification emails do not contain links asking for personal or financial details; fake refund messages commonly lead to phishing sites. Instead, open the CRA's official website yourself to sign in to your CRA account or contact the CRA using an independently verified phone number.

context_text: 20% language-minority threshold for bilingual municipal bylaws is calculated inside each municipality, not provincially. All cities must publish bylaws bilingually regardless of the threshold; s.36 separately addresses bilingual prescribed services. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: Au Nouveau-Brunswick, le seuil de 20 % pour les services municipaux bilingues se calcule-t-il sur l’ensemble de la province?
reference_answer: Non. Le seuil de 20 % se mesure à l'intérieur de chaque municipalité : il concerne la proportion de ses résidents appartenant à la communauté de langue officielle minoritaire, pas la proportion dans l'ensemble du Nouveau-Brunswick. Selon l'article 35 de la Loi sur les langues officielles du Nouveau-Brunswick, une municipalité qui atteint ce seuil doit publier ses arrêtés dans les deux langues; toutes les cités y sont tenues indépendamment du seuil. L'article 36 impose aux collectivités visées l'offre de services et de communications bilingues prescrits par règlement.

context_text: Human Rights Commission accepts eligible federal discrimination claims involving federally regulated banks including foreign authorized banks. Complaints require protected discrimination grounds and jurisdiction/procedure; ordinary bank service disputes may not qualify. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: Would the Canadian Human Rights Commission normally handle a discrimination complaint about a federally regulated bank?
reference_answer: Yes, potentially. The Canadian Human Rights Commission handles admissible discrimination complaints about federally regulated organizations, which explicitly include banks and authorized foreign banks. It must still be a complaint of discrimination under the Canadian Human Rights Act, and the Commission checks whether the matter falls within its jurisdiction, timing and procedural requirements. An ordinary contract or customer-service disagreement without a prohibited discrimination ground may require a different process.

context_text: Accessibility Standards Canada permits anonymous feedback on its accessibility plan. Leave optional name, email and phone fields blank; the agency cannot follow up with anonymous users. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: Puis-je transmettre anonymement à Normes d’accessibilité Canada mes commentaires sur son plan d’accessibilité?
reference_answer: Oui. Normes d'accessibilité Canada accepte les commentaires anonymes sur son plan d'accessibilité. Dans le formulaire de rétroaction, laissez vides les champs facultatifs du nom, de l'adresse courriel et du numéro de téléphone, puis indiquez vos commentaires. L'organisme précise qu'il ne pourra pas vous recontacter au sujet de commentaires transmis anonymement.

context_text: Real risk of significant harm is assessed using sensitivity of personal information and probability of misuse. A breach involving real risk triggers report and notification, while record-keeping remains required even if the risk threshold is not met. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: When deciding whether a data breach poses a real risk of significant harm under PIPEDA, what factors should my organization consider?
reference_answer: Under PIPEDA, assess both the sensitivity of the personal information involved and the probability that the information has been, is being or will be misused, considering the circumstances of the breach. Sensitive data, unauthorized access, malicious intent, evidence of copying and safeguards can affect the assessment. If a breach presents a real risk of significant harm, report it to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner and notify affected individuals as required. A breach below that threshold still has record-keeping obligations.

context_text: A civil union may dissolve through joint notarial declaration if consequences are agreed and children's interests are not at issue. It may also terminate on spouses' marriage to one another or death; otherwise a court judgment may be necessary. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: Au Québec, une union civile doit-elle toujours être dissoute par un tribunal?
reference_answer: Non. Au Québec, une union civile peut être dissoute par une déclaration commune notariée lorsque les conjoints ont réglé les conséquences de leur séparation et que les intérêts de leurs enfants communs ne sont pas en jeu. Sinon, une décision judiciaire est généralement nécessaire. L'union civile est aussi dissoute automatiquement si les conjoints se marient entre eux ou au décès d'un conjoint. Il ne faut donc pas affirmer que le tribunal intervient dans tous les cas.

context_text: Canada Gazette Parts I, II, III in official PDF editions have legal status alongside print from April 1, 2003 onward. Earlier web-hosted issues dated before April 2003 are not retroactively given the same official online status. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: Does the online PDF of the Canada Gazette have official status, or do I need a print copy?
reference_answer: Yes. The online PDF editions of Parts I, II and III of the Canada Gazette published on or after April 1, 2003 have official status alongside the printed editions, so an official PDF can be cited without first finding a paper copy. This statement does not give pre–April 1, 2003 online PDFs the same status merely because they are available on the website.

context_text: For IRPA section 72 judicial-review leave applications the normal filing deadline is 15 days for a matter arising inside Canada, 60 days for a matter arising outside. The clock starts with notice/knowledge and the Federal Court may permit an extension for special reasons; appeal rights generally must be exhausted.
question: Pour demander le contrôle judiciaire d’une décision d’immigration, le délai est-il le même si l’affaire a pris naissance au Canada ou à l’étranger?
reference_answer: Non. Pour une demande d'autorisation et de contrôle judiciaire relevant de l'article 72 de la Loi sur l'immigration et la protection des réfugiés, le délai normal est de 15 jours lorsque l'affaire a pris naissance au Canada, contre 60 jours lorsqu'elle a pris naissance à l'étranger, à compter de l'avis de la décision ou du moment où la personne en a eu connaissance. La Cour fédérale peut, pour des motifs spéciaux, proroger le délai. Il faut vérifier aussi l'épuisement des recours disponibles et les exceptions prévues par la loi.

context_text: OPO awards complaint process addresses eligible federal awards under $34,700 for goods or $139,000 for services. Administration complaint review has different conditions and no dollar threshold; Canadian supplier and timeliness requirements apply. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: My small business has a dispute over the award of a low-value federal contract. What federal office should I check for a complaint process?
reference_answer: Check the Office of the Procurement Ombud (OPO), which has a complaint process for qualifying federal contract awards below specified values. The OPO presently lists an award-complaint limit below $34,700 for goods and below $139,000 for services; eligibility also depends on being a Canadian supplier and meeting filing deadlines and other criteria. Contract-administration complaints follow different threshold rules, so confirm the current limits on the OPO site before submitting.

context_text: A First Nation land code replaces corresponding Indian Act land-management provisions for specified First Nation lands. The code includes First Nation law-making, land use, land interests, financial accountability and dispute resolution rather than removing the Indian Act in full.
question: Que change un code foncier adopté par une Première Nation pour la gestion de ses terres sous le régime de l’accord-cadre?
reference_answer: Dans le régime de l'Accord-cadre relatif à la gestion des terres des Premières Nations, une Première Nation qui adopte son code foncier peut gérer les terres de réserve visées selon ses propres lois, plutôt que sous les dispositions correspondantes de la Loi sur les Indiens. Le code est élaboré et approuvé par la Première Nation; il encadre notamment l'utilisation des terres, la création d'intérêts fonciers, les règles de gestion et la résolution de différends. Il ne supprime pas toute la Loi sur les Indiens et n'étend pas automatiquement l'autorité de la Première Nation à toutes les terres privées.

context_text: Nova Scotia recognized Treaty Day on Tuesday October 1, 2024 after Sept 23–30 Truth and Reconciliation Week. Treaty Day honours treaty relationship and Mi'kmaq contribution; distinct from Sept 30 remembrance of residential school survivors.
question: When did Nova Scotia mark Treaty Day in 2024, and how did it fit with Truth and Reconciliation Week?
reference_answer: Nova Scotia marked Treaty Day on Tuesday, October 1, 2024. It followed Truth and Reconciliation Week, September 23–30, and the September 30 National Day for Truth and Reconciliation. Treaty Day highlights the province's treaty relationship with the Mi'kmaq and their continuing presence, rights and contributions; it is distinct from, although closely connected with, the September 30 remembrance of residential-school survivors.

context_text: The Yukon Umbrella Final Agreement was signed May 29 1993 and supplies the shared framework for later individual First Nations Final Agreements. The UFA is a political framework; the enforceable individual First Nation treaties incorporate UFA provisions plus nation-specific arrangements. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: Dans les revendications territoriales du Yukon, à quoi sert l’Accord-cadre définitif par rapport aux accords propres aux Premières Nations?
reference_answer: L'Accord-cadre définitif du Yukon, signé en 1993 par le Canada, le Yukon et le Conseil des Premières Nations du Yukon, définit les thèmes et principes communs des revendications territoriales. En tant qu'accord-cadre politique, il ne constitue pas à lui seul le traité final juridiquement contraignant d'une Première Nation. Chaque accord définitif propre à une Première Nation en reprend les dispositions et y ajoute des modalités particulières, notamment sur les terres visées, les ressources et les droits de la nation.

context_text: Historical treaty reserve allocations were insufficient for some First Nations, involving federal treaty responsibilities and Saskatchewan's 1930 transfer commitments. TLE settlement agreements support acquisition and transfer of additional land to reserve after settling interests. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: Why are Canada and Saskatchewan involved in treaty land entitlement settlements with First Nations in Saskatchewan?
reference_answer: Canada and Saskatchewan are involved with First Nations because some Saskatchewan First Nations did not receive all the reserve land promised under historical treaties. Canada bears the treaty obligation, while Saskatchewan has related responsibilities under the 1930 Natural Resources Transfer Agreement and the treaty land entitlement settlements. The agreements provide a process for First Nations to obtain land, resolve third-party interests and have the land transferred to reserve status.

context_text: Nunavut Agreement article 5.2.1 establishes Nunavut Wildlife Management Board as an institution of public government. The board undertakes wildlife co-management, considering Inuit harvesting and conservation, even if incorporated as a nonprofit entity. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: L’Accord du Nunavut a-t-il créé le Conseil de gestion des ressources fauniques comme institution publique ou comme organisme privé?
reference_answer: L'Accord du Nunavut, à son article 5.2.1, a établi le Conseil de gestion des ressources fauniques du Nunavut comme une institution de gouvernement public, et non comme un organisme privé. Le Conseil exerce des fonctions de cogestion de la faune dans le cadre de l'Accord, y compris sur des questions liées aux droits de récolte des Inuits et à la conservation des populations animales.

context_text: The Labour Force Survey measures respondents' activity during a one-week reference period, usually the Sunday–Saturday week containing the 15th. December and occasionally November use an earlier reference week; monthly survey estimates are not full-month diaries. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: Does a monthly Labour Force Survey result describe what respondents did throughout the whole month?
reference_answer: No. Monthly Labour Force Survey estimates describe respondents' employment status during a particular reference week—usually the Sunday-to-Saturday week containing the 15th day of the month, with occasional earlier reference weeks near year-end. Interviews generally take place afterward. A result labelled for a month should therefore not be interpreted as tracking each respondent's employment status for every day of that month.

context_text: Yukon Legislative Assembly uses political party labels for MLAs, governing party and opposition caucus. It is a party-based system distinct from NWT consensus governance; party seat totals can change each election. The linked legal, parliamentary, provincial or governmental source directly addresses this requirement.
question: Do members of Yukon’s Legislative Assembly sit under political party labels?
reference_answer: Yes. Unlike the consensus-party-free system used in the Northwest Territories, Yukon's Legislative Assembly operates with party affiliations. Its members may belong to organized political parties, and the governing party, Official Opposition and other party caucuses are identified in Assembly and Yukon government records. The party composition can change after an election, so a stable benchmark should test the system rather than memorize today's seat counts.

context_text: Seasonal adjustment removes recurring seasonal/calendar influences for period-to-period comparison. Adjusted values can differ from raw values and may be revised when new data arrive.
question: Pourquoi utiliser les chiffres désaisonnalisés de Statistique Canada pour comparer deux mois consécutifs?
reference_answer: La désaisonnalisation des séries de Statistique Canada atténue les variations prévisibles qui reviennent à la même période chaque année, comme certaines activités saisonnières, ainsi que des effets du calendrier. Elle permet de mieux comparer deux mois consécutifs et d'identifier une évolution qui ne reflète pas simplement les habitudes saisonnières. Les chiffres désaisonnalisés ne sont pas les valeurs brutes observées et peuvent être révisés à mesure que de nouvelles données arrivent.

context_text: Proposed works may be published in the NPP online registry for public inspection. Certain notices invite Indigenous and public comment, often over 30 days.
question: Where can I look for information on a proposed work in navigable waters when Transport Canada asks the proponent to publish it?
reference_answer: Consult Transport Canada's Navigation Protection Program online registry for the proposed work in navigable waters, where applicable project information and public notices are published. For some works, the proponent uploads details and posts a notice inviting Indigenous peoples and the public to comment, often within a specified 30-day period. The exact notice and decision route depends on the work, waterway and whether the Canadian Navigable Waters Act process requires approval.

context_text: Nests of 18 species retain year-round protection when unoccupied. Abandoned Nest Registry and 12, 24 or 36 months of non-occupation govern designated nests.
question: Le départ des oiseaux suffit-il pour conclure qu’un nid d’oiseau migrateur peut être enlevé au Canada?
reference_answer: Non. Il faut identifier l'espèce et consulter le Règlement sur les oiseaux migrateurs (2022). Les nids de 18 espèces inscrites à l'annexe 1, comme le grand pic, bénéficient d'une protection même lorsqu'ils sont inoccupés. Pour pouvoir enlever ou détruire légalement un nid réputé abandonné de ces espèces, il faut notamment transmettre un avis au Registre des nids abandonnés et respecter la période d'inoccupation applicable à l'espèce : 12, 24 ou 36 mois. Le simple départ des oiseaux n'est pas suffisant.

context_text: Grants are normally non-repayable; student loans are borrowed and repaid. Loans ordinarily enter repayment after six-month non-repayment period following studies.
question: What’s the repayment difference between a Canada Student Grant and a Canada Student Loan?
reference_answer: A Canada Student Grant is generally non-repayable financial aid for eligible students. A Canada Student Loan is borrowed money that must be repaid; federal borrowers normally begin repayment after a six-month non-payment period following the end of studies. Eligibility and changes to enrolment can affect grant conditions, and some provinces and territories administer separate student-aid rules.

context_text: Agreement combines land claims and self-government, effective August 4, 2005. Agreement creates government legislative powers concerning communities, language and resources.
question: L’Accord tłı̨chǫ porte-t-il uniquement sur des terres ou traite-t-il aussi de gouvernance?
reference_answer: Non. L'Accord tłı̨chǫ, entré en vigueur le 4 août 2005, combine un règlement de revendication territoriale et un accord d'autonomie gouvernementale. Il reconnaît des droits sur les terres et les ressources et établit un gouvernement tłı̨chǫ doté de compétences législatives notamment dans les domaines de la culture, de la langue, de l'éducation et de certains services communautaires, sous réserve des limites prévues par l'Accord et par les lois applicables.

context_text: Notice states approved tax years and any expiry. Expiring authorization generally requires reapplication; nonexpiring authorization need not be re-applied every year.
question: How can I tell if CRA approved my disability tax credit for a limited number of years?
reference_answer: Check your CRA disability tax credit notice of determination. It lists the tax years for which you were approved and, where applicable, an expiry date. If there is an expiry date, you will generally need to reapply at the end of the approved period; if the notice has no expiry, you need not reapply unless the CRA asks you to. You can also review your DTC eligibility in your CRA account.

context_text: English/French can be used in federal court proceedings and pleadings. A person's choice of official court language must not disadvantage them.
question: Puis-je présenter des actes de procédure en français devant une cour fédérale au Canada?
reference_answer: Oui. L'article 14(1) de la Loi sur les langues officielles reconnaît le français et l'anglais comme langues officielles des tribunaux fédéraux et permet à toute personne d'utiliser l'une ou l'autre de ces langues dans les actes de procédure, les documents et les instances devant ces tribunaux. Le paragraphe 14(2) précise que ce choix ne doit pas désavantager la personne. Les règles de dépôt et de signification propres au tribunal restent applicables.

context_text: Election-ad transmission is prohibited before local polls close on polling day. Party leader event notices and invitations are specifically excepted from this blackout rule.
question: Can a campaign start transmitting new election ads to the public in a federal riding on polling day while polls are still open there?
reference_answer: Generally no. Section 323(1) of the Canada Elections Act prohibits transmitting election advertising to the public in an electoral district on polling day until all polling stations in that district have closed. The rule concerns election advertising, not every communication by a candidate: section 323(2), for example, excludes a notice of a party leader's event or an invitation to meet or hear that leader from this specific blackout rule. Check the precise content and distribution of the communication.

context_text: Providing money alone is not sufficient to qualify for Canada caregiver amount. Relationship, disability/impairment, income and tax-year criteria determine eligibility.
question: Le seul fait d’aider financièrement un proche suffit-il pour demander le crédit canadien pour aidant naturel?
reference_answer: Non. Le seul fait d'aider financièrement un proche ne rend pas automatiquement admissible au montant canadien pour aidant naturel. Selon la catégorie de demande, la personne aidée doit notamment être votre époux ou conjoint de fait ou une personne à charge admissible ayant une déficience des fonctions physiques ou mentales; le lien familial, le revenu, l'âge et les crédits déjà demandés peuvent modifier l'admissibilité et le montant. Il faut utiliser les conditions de l'année d'imposition concernée.

context_text: Yukon board must offer school-age residents of its education area an educational program consistent with the Yukon Education Act. Board has powers to hire staff and establish locally developed courses. Does not imply board administers every Yukon school.
question: What education is Yukon’s First Nation School Board required to provide to school-age residents of its education area?
reference_answer: Under section 7(a) of Yukon Order-in-Council 2021/15, the Yukon First Nation School Board must provide every school-age person who resides in its education area with an educational program consistent with the Yukon Education Act and regulations. The Board also has powers to run its schools, establish locally developed courses and staff them. This obligation is defined by the Board's education area and applicable education legislation; it should not be interpreted as a mandate to operate every school in Yukon.

context_text: Applying after work permit expiry does not provide maintained work authorization. Normally a person must stop work and seek restoration within 90 days (subject to exceptions), without working while pending.
question: My work permit expired before I applied for an extension. Can I keep working while I apply to restore my status?
reference_answer: No. Applying only after your work permit expired does not give you maintained-status authorization to continue working. You must stop working when the permit expires. If you qualify, you may apply to restore your temporary resident status—generally within 90 days of losing it—and seek a new work permit, but you normally cannot work while the restoration application is being processed. Working again generally requires restored status and a valid work permit or other specific authorization.

context_text: A new Canadian adult passport application requires a guarantor and two references. The guarantor cannot also act as a reference on the same application.
question: Pour une nouvelle demande de passeport canadien, puis-je inscrire mon répondant comme l’une de mes références?
reference_answer: Non. Pour une nouvelle demande de passeport canadien pour adulte, votre répondant ne peut pas aussi être l'une de vos deux références. Le répondant et les personnes de référence servent à confirmer votre identité, mais les rôles doivent être remplis par des personnes distinctes et chacun doit satisfaire aux critères prévus.

context_text: CPP/QPP coordination addresses contributory pension for people who worked in both systems. CRA guidance instructs people who worked in Québec/another province and reside in Québec to contact Retraite Québec.
question: I worked in Ontario and Québec and now live in Québec. Where do I apply for my public contributory retirement pension?
reference_answer: If you contributed to both the Canada Pension Plan and the Québec Pension Plan and currently live in Québec, apply for your public contributory retirement pension through Retraite Québec under the Québec Pension Plan. The CPP and QPP coordinate contributions so time worked in other provinces is not simply lost. Contact Retraite Québec to verify how your contribution record and eligibility are handled.

context_text: A First Nation may negotiate a binding incremental treaty agreement before final treaty conclusion. Incremental agreements offer early benefits but do not replace comprehensive treaty negotiation.
question: Dans le processus de négociation de traités modernes en Colombie-Britannique, une Première Nation peut-elle négocier des ententes progressives en même temps qu’un traité global?
reference_answer: Oui. Dans le processus des traités en Colombie-Britannique, une Première Nation peut négocier un traité global tout en concluant, en parallèle, des accords progressifs ou sectoriels sur des questions particulières, comme des transferts de terres, des revenus liés aux ressources ou des compétences de gouvernance. Ces accords peuvent produire des résultats avant le traité global, sans nécessairement régler toutes les questions territoriales ou constitutionnelles.

context_text: RSCs coordinate regional solid-waste services, disposal, recycling and long-term planning. The regional approach supports shared infrastructure and avoids duplicating facilities and expenditures.
question: Pourquoi les commissions de services régionaux du Nouveau-Brunswick interviennent-elles dans la gestion des déchets solides?
reference_answer: Au Nouveau-Brunswick, les commissions de services régionaux planifient, coordonnent et supervisent les systèmes régionaux de gestion des déchets solides. Elles organisent notamment l'élimination des déchets, certaines activités de recyclage et la planification des infrastructures à long terme pour plusieurs collectivités. Cette mise en commun peut réduire les coûts et améliorer la cohérence des services, sans faire de la commission un palier de gouvernement local distinct.

context_text: Extra-billing and patient charges for insured services trigger dollar-for-dollar CHT deductions. Reimbursement can follow removal of charges and correction of underlying causes.
question: Why does the federal government care if a province lets doctors extra-bill for insured health services?
reference_answer: Under sections 18–21 of the Canada Health Act, extra-billing and user charges for insured services can trigger mandatory, dollar-for-dollar reductions in the province's Canada Health Transfer. The federal government uses this funding condition to support reasonable access to medically necessary insured services without charges to patients. A province can potentially be reimbursed under federal reimbursement policy if it eliminates the prohibited charges and addresses their causes.

context_text: Federal Acts default to coming into force on royal assent when no commencement provision exists. Specific deferred or section-specific commencement rules can override that default.
question: Si une loi fédérale ne prévoit aucune date d’entrée en vigueur, quelle date dois-je utiliser?
reference_answer: À défaut de disposition fixant une date d'entrée en vigueur dans une loi fédérale, celle-ci entre en vigueur à la date de la sanction royale. C'est la règle supplétive du paragraphe 5(2) de la Loi d'interprétation; il faut toutefois vérifier si la loi ou certaines dispositions prévoient une date ultérieure ou une entrée en vigueur par décret.

context_text: Generally candidates collect 100 qualified electors' signatures in the riding. Schedule 3 ridings require 50 signatures, with witnessing rules.
question: Do I need the same number of signatures to run federally in every riding?
reference_answer: No. Under federal election nomination rules, most candidates need signatures from at least 100 qualified electors living in their electoral district. Candidates in the large or remote electoral districts listed in Schedule 3 of the Canada Elections Act need at least 50. The signatures must be witnessed as Elections Canada requires.

context_text: Once registered to vote by special ballot, voters cannot vote another way in the same election. Special-ballot mailing/receipt deadlines must be met; registration is not interchangeable with polling place voting.
question: Si ma demande de vote par bulletin spécial a été acceptée, puis-je finalement voter à mon bureau de scrutin?
reference_answer: En règle générale, non. Une fois qu’Élections Canada a accepté votre demande de vote par bulletin spécial, vous êtes inscrit pour voter de cette façon à cette élection fédérale et devez retourner votre bulletin spécial avant la date limite prescrite. Vous ne pouvez pas simplement choisir de voter plutôt à un bureau de scrutin ordinaire. Si une situation exceptionnelle vous empêche d’utiliser le bulletin spécial, communiquez avec Élections Canada pour connaître les procédures applicables à cette élection, au lieu de présumer que vous pouvez déposer un autre bulletin.

context_text: A landlord notice alone does not evict a tenant protected by the Residential Tenancies Act. Landlord must obtain a Landlord and Tenant Board eviction order; enforcement belongs to Sheriff.
question: In Ontario, can my landlord evict me just by handing me an eviction notice?
reference_answer: No. For an Ontario residential tenancy covered by the Residential Tenancies Act, a landlord's notice of termination does not itself evict the tenant. The landlord generally must apply to the Landlord and Tenant Board and obtain an eviction order; only the Court Enforcement Office (Sheriff) may enforce an eviction. The tenant can normally remain while the matter is heard, subject to applicable legal orders and deadlines.

context_text: Unattainable prices caused by mandatory seller-imposed fixed fees may violate Competition Act. Mandatory charges imposed on buyers by law, such as sales taxes, are distinguishable from seller fees.
question: Un site affiche un prix que je ne peux obtenir sans payer des frais fixes obligatoires. Est-ce la même chose qu’une taxe de vente ajoutée à la caisse?
reference_answer: Non. Dans le droit canadien de la concurrence, l'affichage d'un prix impossible à obtenir parce que des frais fixes obligatoires s'y ajoutent peut constituer une indication de prix au compte-gouttes. L'exception légale vise certains frais réellement imposés à l'acheteur par une loi fédérale ou provinciale, comme les taxes de vente; des frais obligatoires inventés par le vendeur ne deviennent pas des taxes du seul fait qu'ils figurent séparément.

context_text: Canadian competition enforcement considers both literal meaning and general impression of an advertisement. A technically correct standalone phrase can be misleading in the overall material impression.
question: Can an ad be misleading under Canadian competition law even if its individual words are technically true?
reference_answer: Yes. Under the Competition Act, an advertisement can be materially misleading even if each individual statement is literally true. The assessment considers both the general impression conveyed to an ordinary audience and the literal meaning of the claims. The overall presentation, omitted context or qualifying fine print can create a deceptive impression.

context_text: An early-termination-fee wireless contract has a trial of at least 15 calendar days. An eligible customer self-identifying with a disability has 30 days and at least twice standard trial use limits.
question: Quelle différence le Code sur les services sans fil prévoit-il pour la période d’essai d’une personne handicapée?
reference_answer: Selon le Code sur les services sans fil du CRTC, une personne qui s'identifie comme handicapée bénéficie d'une période d'essai d'au moins 30 jours civils, comparativement à au moins 15 jours pour la période ordinaire lorsque le contrat prévoit des frais de résiliation anticipée. Elle doit également pouvoir utiliser au moins le double des quantités permises durant la période ordinaire, sans dépasser les conditions de retour de l'appareil en état presque neuf, avec l'emballage d'origine, le cas échéant.

context_text: A covered internet contract with early cancellation fee gets a trial period of at least 15 calendar days. Customers self-identifying as disabled get minimum 30 days; usage/equipment return requirements apply.
question: My home internet contract has an early cancellation fee. What minimum trial period does the CRTC Internet Code give me if my provider is covered?
reference_answer: For a new home-Internet contract covered by the CRTC Internet Code and subject to an early cancellation fee, the standard trial period is at least 15 calendar days from the start of service. If you self-identify as a person with a disability, the minimum is 30 days. Cancellation without penalty during the trial depends on staying within permitted usage and returning provided equipment in near-new condition, including original packaging where applicable. The Internet Code applies directly to specified major ISPs, so check provider coverage.

context_text: The landlord must perform and record condition inspection and offer tenant proper participation. Both normally sign the inspection report; statutory process also covers tenant nonparticipation after opportunities.
question: En Colombie-Britannique, qui doit normalement remplir le rapport d’inspection de l’état du logement et le signer?
reference_answer: En Colombie-Britannique, le locateur doit organiser l'inspection de l'état du logement avec le locataire et remplir un rapport d'inspection écrit. Le formulaire doit prévoir les signatures du locateur et du locataire ainsi que la possibilité pour le locataire de signaler son désaccord avec l'évaluation. Si l'inspection n'a pas pu se tenir ou si le locataire refuse de signer, les règles de convocation et de preuve s'appliquent; l'absence d'une signature ne permet pas d'ignorer la procédure.

context_text: Denied boarding concerns passengers with valid tickets and check-ins exceeding the seats available. Refusal for missing documents is distinct and is governed by carrier rules; air-passenger protections differ.
question: Is being denied boarding because there aren’t enough seats treated the same as being refused transport for missing documents?
reference_answer: No. Under Canada's Air Passenger Protection framework, denied boarding (bumping) generally means more checked-in passengers with valid tickets than available seats, often because of overbooking or an aircraft change. Refusal to transport because a traveller lacks required documents is a different category governed by the carrier's applicable tariff and travel rules. Rights to compensation or assistance may differ significantly.

context_text: A carrier can request a declaration of individual service-dog training when a booking is made. Before departure it can seek identification/training document from qualified trainer, with accessibility accommodations.
question: Pour voyager avec mon chien d’assistance auprès d’un transporteur visé par le règlement fédéral, quel justificatif pourrait-on me demander?
reference_answer: Pour voyager avec un chien d'assistance auprès d'un transporteur assujetti au règlement fédéral, celui-ci peut demander, lors de la réservation, une déclaration attestant que le chien a reçu une formation individuelle auprès d'un organisme ou d'une personne spécialisée afin d'accomplir une tâche liée au handicap. Avant le départ, il peut aussi exiger une carte d'identité ou un autre document de cet organisme ou formateur, identifiant la personne et attestant la formation. Les voyageurs peuvent discuter avec le transporteur des moyens de transmettre le justificatif.

context_text: CFIA posts food recalls even when no distinct public Food Recall Warning was issued. High-risk incidents trigger public warning; lower-risk notices may appear without such warning.
question: Does the CFIA issue a public warning for every food recall?
reference_answer: No. The Canadian Food Inspection Agency publishes recall records, but it does not issue a separate public Food Recall Warning for every recall. It considers the product's risk, where it was distributed and whether consumers need to act; some lower-risk recalls may be posted without a separate public warning. A recall and a public warning are distinct steps, and the absence of a warning does not by itself prove that no recall occurred.

context_text: A drug DIN is an eight-digit identifier assigned before marketing to an authorised drug. DIN identifies manufacturer, product name, active ingredients, strengths, dosage form and route.
question: Que signifie le numéro DIN à huit chiffres sur un médicament vendu au Canada?
reference_answer: Le DIN (numéro d'identification du médicament) est un code unique à huit chiffres attribué par Santé Canada à un produit pharmaceutique autorisé avant sa mise en marché. Il identifie notamment le fabricant, le nom du produit, les ingrédients actifs, leur concentration, la forme pharmaceutique et la voie d'administration. Il figure sur l'étiquette des médicaments d'ordonnance et de nombreux médicaments vendus sans ordonnance.

context_text: The 2026–27 plan focuses on French-language government services for Acadian and francophone Nova Scotians. The plan specifically coordinates and expands post-secondary services and does not promise all courses in French. Official French title is ministère de l’Éducation postsecondaire, not ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur. Nova Scotia plan prioritizes Acadian and francophone community needs and accessible coordinated services. Catalog outlines objectives generally; exact qualifications in linked PDF not independently visually verified this pass. Text describes inclusive access, French-language documents, coordination with Université Sainte-Anne and service improvements.
question: Selon son plan de services en français 2026–2027, quel public le ministère de l’Éducation postsecondaire de la Nouvelle-Écosse cherche-t-il à mieux servir?
reference_answer: Le ministère de l’Éducation postsecondaire cherche à mieux servir la communauté acadienne et francophone de la Nouvelle-Écosse, notamment les apprenants et partenaires du postsecondaire qui ont besoin de services et de renseignements en français. Le plan vise à améliorer l’accessibilité et la coordination de ces services, avec des partenaires comme l’Université Sainte-Anne. Il ne garantit pas que tous les programmes postsecondaires seront offerts en français.

context_text: Licensed natural health products carry eight-digit NPN or DIN-HM. The number signals market authorization under recommended conditions, not absence of every risk.
question: What number should I look for on the label to tell whether a natural health product is licensed for sale in Canada?
reference_answer: Look for the eight-digit Natural Product Number (NPN) on the label of a licensed natural health product in Canada, or an eight-digit Homeopathic Medicine Number (DIN-HM) if it is a licensed homeopathic product. These numbers indicate Health Canada authorization for marketing under applicable rules, not a guarantee that the product is risk-free or suitable for every individual.

context_text: CIPO does not check the truth of ownership or originality claims on registration. Copyright certificate is rebuttable ownership evidence, not an unchallengeable conclusion.
question: Quand l’Office de la propriété intellectuelle traite une demande d’enregistrement de droit d’auteur, vérifie-t-il que le demandeur est bien titulaire du droit?
reference_answer: Non. L'Office de la propriété intellectuelle du Canada peut enregistrer la demande de droit d'auteur sans vérifier si les affirmations du demandeur sur la titularité ou l'originalité de l'œuvre sont exactes. Le certificat d'enregistrement constitue une preuve présumée du droit et de la titularité au sens de la Loi sur le droit d'auteur, mais cette présomption peut être contestée devant un tribunal.

context_text: Registration lasts ten years from date of grant. Renewal for subsequent ten-year terms requires applicable fee.
question: Once my Canadian trademark is registered, do I have to renew it to keep the registration active?
reference_answer: Yes. A Canadian trademark registration normally lasts ten years from its date of registration. To keep the registration active, the owner must pay the required fee and renew it for subsequent ten-year terms; the Canadian Intellectual Property Office administers renewals. Check the actual registration and renewal deadlines, especially for historical registrations issued under earlier rules.

context_text: Lobbying Act public office holder can be elected or appointed. It covers Members, senators, parliamentary staff and federal employees; designated subgroup is narrower.
question: Dans le régime fédéral de lobbying, un titulaire de charge publique peut-il être une personne élue ou seulement une personne nommée?
reference_answer: Dans le régime fédéral de lobbying, un titulaire d'une charge publique peut être une personne élue ou nommée. Le terme vise notamment les députés, les sénateurs, leur personnel et des fonctionnaires fédéraux. Il ne faut pas le confondre avec la catégorie plus restreinte des titulaires d'une charge publique désignée, pour laquelle des exigences supplémentaires peuvent s'appliquer.

context_text: Manitoba Ombudsman handles provincial public-body access and privacy complaints. Its process includes access refusals, delays, personal-information correction and privacy concerns.
question: Who can I contact about making a complaint under Manitoba’s Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act?
reference_answer: For a complaint about a Manitoba provincial public body's response to an access-to-information request or its handling of personal information under the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (FIPPA), contact Manitoba Ombudsman. The Ombudsman's office can investigate whether the authority complied with FIPPA, explain complaint procedures and relevant timing, and recommend corrective action. It is not the same as a private-sector privacy complaint under federal PIPEDA.

context_text: Reporting public office holder declares a recusal within 60 days. Declaration identifies the conflict that was avoided.
question: How long does a reporting public office holder have to publicly declare a recusal under the federal Conflict of Interest Act?
reference_answer: Under subsection 25(1) of the federal Conflict of Interest Act, a reporting public office holder who recuses themself to avoid a conflict of interest must publicly declare the recusal within 60 days after it takes place. The declaration must contain enough detail to identify the conflict avoided. The requirement applies specifically to reporting public office holders, not automatically to every person employed by a government agency.

context_text: Federal public servant can disclose wrongdoing to supervisor, senior officer or Integrity Commissioner. Direct disclosure to Integrity Commissioner need not await exhaustion of internal channels.
question: Un fonctionnaire fédéral doit-il signaler un acte répréhensible uniquement à son superviseur?
reference_answer: Non. La Loi sur la protection des fonctionnaires divulgateurs d'actes répréhensibles offre plusieurs voies de signalement : le fonctionnaire peut notamment s'adresser à son superviseur, à l'agent supérieur chargé des divulgations dans son organisation, ou directement au Commissariat à l'intégrité du secteur public du Canada. Il faut vérifier la nature de l'acte allégué et les règles de confidentialité et de protection contre les représailles.

context_text: Public-service employee must receive Public Service Commission permission before publicly declaring intent to become municipal election candidate. PSC evaluates perceived/actual political impartiality and may impose leave conditions. Direct official law or agency page supports specific claim.
question: I’m a federal public servant thinking of running for municipal office. Can I announce it publicly before getting permission?
reference_answer: No. A federal public-service employee who is subject to the Public Service Employment Act's political-activities regime must request and receive permission from the Public Service Commission before publicly declaring an intention to be a candidate in a municipal, provincial, territorial or federal election. The Commission assesses the risk to political impartiality and may impose conditions. A public announcement or seeking nomination before permission can breach the rules.

context_text: Federal workers cannot refuse under s128 when refusal directly endangers another person's life, health or safety. A second s128(2) exception concerns danger that is a normal condition of employment; hazard reporting process still applies. Direct official law or agency page supports specific claim.
question: Dans un milieu de travail sous réglementation fédérale, puis-je refuser un travail dangereux si mon refus met directement une autre personne en danger?
reference_answer: Non, pas dans cette situation précise. Le paragraphe 128(2) du Code canadien du travail prévoit que l'employé ne peut exercer le droit de refuser un travail dangereux si ce refus met directement en danger la vie, la santé ou la sécurité d'une autre personne. Une autre exception vise un danger qui constitue une condition normale de l'emploi, tel que défini par la jurisprudence et les directives. Cela ne supprime pas le droit de signaler le danger ni les obligations de sécurité de l'employeur.

context_text: Yukon Ombudsman cannot normally investigate individual complaints against municipalities or Yukon First Nation governments. The Ombudsman may investigate those bodies at the municipal or First Nation government's request. Direct official law or agency page supports specific claim.
question: L’ombudsman du Yukon peut-il enquêter sur une plainte contre une municipalité du territoire?
reference_answer: En règle générale, non. L'Ombudsman du Yukon ne peut pas enquêter, sur la plainte d'une personne seule, contre une municipalité ou un gouvernement de Première Nation du Yukon : ces organismes ne relèvent pas habituellement de son mandat. Il peut toutefois mener une enquête si la municipalité ou le gouvernement de Première Nation concerné le lui demande. Il faut utiliser d'abord les mécanismes de plainte propres à l'organisme.

context_text: For death of immediate family, federally regulated employees get up to 10 days of bereavement leave. After three consecutive months employment first three days are paid; other leave is ordinarily unpaid, with separate child-death provisions. Direct official law or agency page supports specific claim.
question: I work for a federally regulated employer. Is all of my bereavement leave necessarily paid?
reference_answer: No. Under the ordinary federal bereavement-leave minimum, an employee in a federally regulated workplace may have up to 10 days of leave after the death of an immediate family member, but only the first three days are paid if they have completed three consecutive months of continuous employment. Remaining days are normally unpaid under the federal minimum; more generous collective agreements or employer benefits may apply. Distinct rules can apply to the death of a child.

context_text: Federal labour standards unjust-dismissal complaint deadline is normally 90 days after date of dismissal. Eligible claimant generally must have 12 consecutive months service, be outside collective agreement and not be a manager. Direct official law or agency page supports specific claim.
question: Quel est le délai habituel pour déposer une plainte de congédiement injuste auprès du Programme du travail fédéral?
reference_answer: Pour une plainte de congédiement injuste relevant de la partie III du Code canadien du travail, le délai normal est de 90 jours suivant la date du congédiement. L'admissibilité dépend aussi, entre autres, d'au moins douze mois de service continu, de l'absence de convention collective applicable et du fait de ne pas occuper un poste de gestion. Une prorogation de délai peut être possible dans les cas prévus par le processus.

context_text: A federal wage complaint is generally due within six months after pay was owed. Unjust-dismissal complaints have a separate 90-day deadline.
question: How soon should I file a federal labour standards complaint about wages that were due but never paid?
reference_answer: A federal labour-standards complaint seeking unpaid wages or similar monetary amounts is generally due within six months after the last day the federally regulated employer was required to pay the money. This is a different period from the 90 days used for unjust-dismissal complaints. Verify the exact due date for the wages and any available extension provisions.

context_text: Minimum federal individual-termination notice after four completed years is four weeks. Employer may provide pay instead of notice, or combine notice and payment.
question: Après quatre ans de service continu, quel préavis minimal s’applique normalement à un licenciement individuel sous le régime fédéral, sans motif valable?
reference_answer: Pour un licenciement individuel sans motif valable, après quatre années complètes de service continu dans un emploi sous réglementation fédérale, le préavis écrit minimal est normalement de quatre semaines. L'employeur peut verser une indemnité tenant lieu de préavis ou combiner préavis et indemnité. Les autres obligations, notamment l'indemnité de départ après douze mois de service, doivent être examinées séparément.

context_text: NWT Languages Commissioner handles Official Languages Act complaints. Office encourages trying to resolve a language service problem with the institution first.
question: Who can investigate an official-language complaint involving a Northwest Territories government department?
reference_answer: If you believe a Government of the Northwest Territories department has violated rights under the territorial Official Languages Act, contact the independent Languages Commissioner of the Northwest Territories. The office receives and investigates language-rights complaints, makes recommendations and reports on systemic issues. Its guidance generally encourages first attempting to resolve the issue with the department, without removing the right to file a complaint.

context_text: RCMP contract policing agreements cover eight provinces and three territories. Ontario and Québec operate their own provincial police forces.
question: Quelles provinces ont leur propre police provinciale plutôt qu’un contrat provincial de services policiers avec la GRC?
reference_answer: L'Ontario et le Québec ont leurs propres forces de police provinciales, respectivement la Police provinciale de l'Ontario et la Sûreté du Québec, plutôt que le service de police provincial fourni par contrat par la GRC dans les huit autres provinces. La GRC continue néanmoins d'exercer des responsabilités de police fédérale et de sécurité nationale en Ontario et au Québec.

context_text: TSB independently investigates rail and other transport occurrences for safety. TSB is not authorized to assign civil or criminal liability for transport accidents.
question: Does the Transportation Safety Board decide who is legally liable for a rail accident?
reference_answer: No. The Transportation Safety Board of Canada independently investigates selected air, marine, pipeline and rail occurrences to determine what happened and why, identify safety deficiencies and make safety recommendations. It does not assign legal fault or determine civil or criminal liability for an accident. Those legal questions belong to other processes and authorities.

context_text: Pipelines crossing provincial or international boundaries are generally regulated federally by CER. Pipelines contained within one province are generally overseen by provincial regulators. Official primary-source text supports this requirement.
question: Un oléoduc qui traverse une frontière provinciale relève-t-il du même régime qu’un oléoduc entièrement situé dans une province?
reference_answer: Non. Un oléoduc qui traverse une frontière provinciale relève généralement de la Régie de l'énergie du Canada, dans le cadre fédéral applicable aux pipelines interprovinciaux et internationaux. Un oléoduc entièrement situé dans une seule province relève en règle générale de l'organisme provincial compétent, mais la qualification juridique de certaines installations peut nécessiter un examen particulier.

context_text: CNSC has a table of facilities currently licensed or with applications under review across Canada. Table shows province, facility name, status such as operating/decommissioning/application, and licensee. Official primary-source text supports this requirement.
question: Where can I check whether a Canadian nuclear facility is listed as operating or has a licence application under review?
reference_answer: Consult the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission's online 'Nuclear facilities in Canada' listing. It identifies regulated nuclear facilities, their province, licensee and current status—for example operating, decommissioning or licence application under review. Because facility licensing status changes, confirm the date and, where necessary, open the facility's detailed CNSC page before relying on it.

context_text: Inuktut Protection Act s3 extends availability obligations to private-sector organizations and public bodies. Required public communications include signage, commercial advertising and client services, with conditions set in law. Official primary-source text supports this requirement.
question: L’obligation d’afficher en inuktut au Nunavut concerne-t-elle aussi les entreprises privées?
reference_answer: Oui. Au Nunavut, l'article 3 de la Loi sur la protection de la langue inuit s'applique notamment aux organisations privées qui offrent des services au public, ainsi qu'aux institutions publiques. Elles doivent mettre l'inuktut à disposition dans les affiches publiques, panneaux, publicités et certains services destinés à la clientèle. Les modalités linguistiques précises, y compris le choix entre inuktitut et inuinnaqtun selon la collectivité, doivent être vérifiées dans le texte réglementaire et les directives du commissaire.

context_text: Canada's water governance is shared among federal, provincial, municipal, territorial and Indigenous governments. Provinces commonly license water use; federal responsibilities include fisheries, navigation and boundary waters. Official primary-source text supports this requirement.
question: Is water management in Canada the responsibility of one level of government?
reference_answer: No. Water management in Canada is a shared responsibility. Provinces generally administer water resources and many licensing and land-use matters within their boundaries; the federal government has responsibilities in areas such as fisheries, navigation, transboundary waters and water-quality monitoring. Municipalities often operate water and wastewater services, while territories and Indigenous governments have authority under their own arrangements. The responsible institution depends on the issue, location and applicable law.

context_text: Listing a hazardous substance alone does not trigger all requirements; concentration thresholds and exclusions affect coverage. On-site amount and container-system capacity influence whether notification or full environmental emergency planning is required. Official primary-source text supports this requirement.
question: La simple présence d’une substance sur la liste fédérale des urgences environnementales signifie-t-elle que toute quantité détenue déclenche les mêmes obligations?
reference_answer: Non. Dans le Règlement sur les urgences environnementales (2019), la simple inscription d'une substance à l'annexe 1 n'entraîne pas toutes les obligations pour toute quantité. Il faut notamment tenir compte de la concentration minimale inscrite pour la substance, de la quantité totale et de la capacité du plus grand système de conteneurs, ainsi que des exclusions prévues. Les obligations de déclaration, de planification et de notification peuvent avoir des conditions de déclenchement distinctes.

context_text: ECCC publishes proposed/active pollution-prevention notices and results. Notice list describes objectives, target sectors, and performance where available.
question: Where can I find the federal pollution prevention planning notices and see how they performed?
reference_answer: Use Environment and Climate Change Canada's online 'List of pollution prevention planning notices and their performance.' It links notices issued under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act and describes resulting performance information. For a given substance or industry, check the relevant notice and performance report rather than assuming one notice applies to every facility.

context_text: CEPA healthy environment framework guides designated federal CEPA actions. It does not govern every federal/provincial environmental decision.
question: Le cadre fédéral sur le droit à un environnement sain vise-t-il toutes les décisions environnementales au Canada?
reference_answer: Non. Le cadre fédéral de mise en œuvre du droit à un environnement sain explique comment Environnement et Changement climatique Canada et Santé Canada doivent tenir compte de ce droit dans l'application de la Loi canadienne sur la protection de l'environnement (1999), telle que modifiée en 2023. Il ne constitue pas un régime général qui s'applique indistinctement à toutes les décisions environnementales fédérales, provinciales ou municipales. Le droit reconnu par cette loi est soumis aux limites raisonnables qu'elle prévoit.

context_text: A researcher must request restricted Saskatchewan archive records for review under applicable privacy law. Saskatchewan archives may redact protected content or use a confidentiality agreement.
question: Can I automatically see any restricted record held by the Provincial Archives of Saskatchewan?
reference_answer: No. Holding a record does not mean the Provincial Archives of Saskatchewan can release it automatically. Access to restricted records must be reviewed under Saskatchewan privacy and access legislation, relevant health-information law and donor agreements. Researchers should submit a request for the particular restricted material; staff review for protected information, may sever restricted passages, or sometimes use a confidentiality undertaking.

context_text: Canadian Coast Guard conducts maritime SAR on federally controlled waterways. Maritime SAR coordinates communications and rescue centres with partners.
question: What kind of search and rescue is the Canadian Coast Guard responsible for?
reference_answer: The Canadian Coast Guard is responsible for maritime search-and-rescue services on federally controlled waterways. With the Canadian Armed Forces and other partners, it responds to people and vessels in distress, provides marine alerts and communications, and coordinates through joint rescue coordination centres and maritime rescue sub-centres. Canada's overall SAR system has three regions—Halifax, Trenton and Victoria—but that does not mean the Coast Guard is solely responsible for all land or aviation rescues.

context_text: The NRC clock display derives official time from NRC atomic clocks using time-stamped messages and network delay correction. NRC says some timezone information outdated since Nov 1 2026, so regional legal settings need independent check.
question: D’où vient l’heure affichée sur l’horloge Web officielle du Conseil national de recherches du Canada?
reference_answer: L'heure affichée par l'horloge Web officielle du Conseil national de recherches du Canada (CNRC) est fondée sur les horloges atomiques du CNRC, qui servent de référence pour l'heure officielle canadienne. Le navigateur reçoit des messages horodatés et l'affichage tient compte du délai de communication mesuré.

context_text: Legal deposit eligible Canadian publications are submitted to Library and Archives Canada. Legal deposit preserves documentary heritage and eligibility varies by format.
question: What is legal deposit for Canadian publications, and which federal institution receives them?
reference_answer: Legal deposit is the statutory requirement for Canadian publishers and producers to submit eligible published materials to Library and Archives Canada (LAC). It helps preserve Canada's published documentary heritage in the national collection for long-term access and research. The forms and number of copies depend on the material and publication format; not every informal draft or document falls under legal deposit.

context_text: OGL Canada permits copying, modifying, distributing and even commercial reuse of licensed information. Redistribution requires source attribution using provider's wording or default attribution; licence link where possible.
question: Puis-je réutiliser des données sous la Licence du gouvernement ouvert du Canada sans citer la source?
reference_answer: Non. La Licence du gouvernement ouvert – Canada permet notamment de copier, modifier, distribuer et publier l'information, y compris à des fins commerciales, mais elle exige de reconnaître la source. Il faut reprendre la mention d'attribution prévue par le fournisseur et, si possible, fournir un lien vers la licence. Si aucune mention précise n'est fournie, la licence indique une mention d'attribution de rechange. Cette licence ne couvre pas automatiquement toute information affichée sur un site gouvernemental.

context_text: Information and Privacy Commissioner is independent mechanism for reviewing provincial ATIPPA access refusals. Complaints can also concern fees, correction of personal information and misuse of protected information.
question: À Terre-Neuve-et-Labrador, à quel organisme indépendant puis-je demander la révision d’une décision provinciale d’accès à l’information?
reference_answer: À Terre-Neuve-et-Labrador, le Commissariat à l'information et à la protection de la vie privée (Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner) est l'organisme indépendant à qui une personne peut demander la révision d'une décision d'accès à l'information prise sous l'Access to Information and Protection of Privacy Act, 2015. La demande doit respecter la procédure et les délais applicables; le commissaire examine notamment les refus d'accès ou les réponses jugées insuffisantes.

context_text: Canada Gazette Part I publishes notices and proposed regulations. Part II publishes official regulations after making/registration; draft proposals are not inherently final.
question: If I’m tracking a federal regulatory proposal, what’s the difference between looking in Part I and Part II of the Canada Gazette?
reference_answer: Canada Gazette, Part I generally publishes government notices, proposed federal regulations and other documents for consultation; Part II publishes regulations and other statutory instruments once made or registered, together with related explanatory material. For a proposal and its eventual adopted text, consult Part I and later Part II, but don't presume every Part I proposal was adopted unchanged.

context_text: Election proposal costing is available on request from recognized parties or independent MPs during relevant election period. The usual fixed-date window starts 120 days before election, or after dissolution for early election.
question: Dans quelles circonstances le directeur parlementaire du budget offre-t-il un service d’évaluation du coût des propositions électorales fédérales?
reference_answer: Dans le régime prévu par la Loi sur le Parlement du Canada, le directeur parlementaire du budget (DPB) peut établir le coût de certaines propositions électorales à la demande d'un parti politique reconnu ou d'un député indépendant pendant la période pertinente. Cette période comprend normalement les 120 jours précédant une élection fédérale à date fixe ou, pour une élection anticipée, la période débutant à la dissolution du Parlement. Le service exige une demande conforme aux règles et concerne des propositions chiffrables; il n'évalue pas automatiquement toutes les promesses.

context_text: Office of Auditor General conducts the audit of annual Consolidated Financial Statements of Government of Canada. Auditor General gives an independent audit opinion reported in the Public Accounts.
question: Who audits the consolidated financial statements of the Government of Canada?
reference_answer: The Office of the Auditor General of Canada, headed by the Auditor General, audits the consolidated financial statements of the Government of Canada as part of the annual Public Accounts. The Auditor General gives an independent audit opinion on whether those statements are fairly presented in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework.

context_text: Statutory Instruments Act imposes general examination, registration and publication requirements on regulations. Specific exemptions in enabling legislation or statutory instrument rules can alter those steps; check legal authority.
question: Dans la préparation d’un règlement fédéral, pourquoi faut-il vérifier si le texte habilitant prévoit une exemption à la Loi sur les textes réglementaires?
reference_answer: Parce que la Loi sur les textes réglementaires prévoit des exigences ordinaires comme l'examen juridique, l'enregistrement et la publication de certains textes réglementaires. Si la loi habilitante exempte expressément un instrument de tout ou partie de ces exigences, le parcours réglementaire change. Le Guide de rédaction fédéral insiste pour que les instructions précisent l'autorité légale de toute exemption souhaitée et la justifient, notamment par un autre moyen de communiquer le texte aux personnes touchées.

context_text: Section 93 makes municipal CAO head of administration with duty to implement council resolutions. Section 93 requires safeguarding official records and accurate municipal money/assets/liabilities accounting. Official consolidation current to November 29 2023; potential later amendments not checked.
question: In a PEI municipal government, what does the chief administrative officer do with the municipality’s records and finances?
reference_answer: In Prince Edward Island, the municipal chief administrative officer (CAO) is responsible for implementing council decisions and administering the municipality. Under the Municipal Government Act, the CAO safeguards municipal books and records, ensures proper accounting for money received and disbursed, maintains accurate records of assets and liabilities, prepares financial information for council, and ensures financial statements are produced and audited as required. Council sets policy while the CAO supervises daily administration.

context_text: Service Canada no longer issues replacement plastic Social Insurance Number cards. A Confirmation of SIN document or online MSCA access can provide proof of an existing number.
question: I lost my old plastic SIN card. Can Service Canada issue another plastic card?
reference_answer: No. Service Canada stopped issuing replacement plastic Social Insurance Number (SIN) cards. If you lose your old card or need proof of your number, you can request a Confirmation of SIN in paper or digital format, or view and print your SIN through My Service Canada Account. Protect the number because the identifier remains valid even if the card is gone.

context_text: Maternity benefits reserved for the person who is pregnant or gave birth. Parental benefits are distinct and may be shared.
question: Mon conjoint peut-il toucher les prestations de maternité de l’assurance-emploi à ma place?
reference_answer: Non. Les prestations de maternité de l'assurance-emploi sont réservées à la personne qui cesse de travailler parce qu'elle est enceinte ou vient d'accoucher; elles ne peuvent pas être partagées avec le conjoint ou l'autre parent. Les prestations parentales constituent un programme distinct qui peut être partagé entre les parents admissibles. Les personnes résidant au Québec sont généralement couvertes par le Régime québécois d'assurance parentale plutôt que les prestations fédérales de maternité et parentales.

context_text: EI sickness medical certificate confirms unable to work for medical reasons. Certificate provides approximate duration, separate eligibility rules still apply.
question: What does the medical certificate for EI sickness benefits need to say?
reference_answer: For Employment Insurance sickness benefits, a medical certificate must state that a medical condition prevents you from working and give the approximate period of time you are unable to work. A qualified medical practitioner must provide the certificate; conditions can include injury, illness or quarantine. The certificate alone does not guarantee EI eligibility, which also depends on employment and insured-hour rules.

context_text: A severe CPP disability prevents regular work at any job. A prolonged CPP disability is long-term, not expected to recover, or likely to cause death. Statutory/administrative definition checked on current federal page.
question: Pour les prestations d’invalidité du RPC, que veulent dire « grave » et « prolongée »?
reference_answer: Pour l'invalidité du Régime de pensions du Canada (RPC), « grave » signifie qu'une déficience physique ou mentale empêche une personne d'exercer régulièrement une occupation véritablement rémunératrice. « Prolongée » signifie que l'invalidité risque de durer pendant une période longue, continue et indéfinie ou d'entraîner le décès. Les deux conditions doivent être satisfaites et le RPC vérifie aussi les cotisations exigées.

context_text: An Ontario photo health card cannot ordinarily be renewed online within 90 days after the holder changes their address with ServiceOntario. In-person renewal remains an option if the applicant satisfies ServiceOntario identity and renewal criteria. Current official agency guidance independently checked for this material claim.
question: I just changed my address with ServiceOntario. Can I renew my Ontario health card online this week?
reference_answer: Not through the ordinary online health-card renewal service this week. Ontario says you cannot renew your Ontario health card online within 90 days after changing your address with ServiceOntario. You may renew in person at a ServiceOntario centre if you otherwise qualify; check that your current health card or photo identification meets the applicable requirements.

context_text: A person living outside Canada normally needs at least 20 years of residence in Canada after age 18 to receive an Old Age Security pension. A bilateral social-security agreement can help meet the OAS residence qualifying period through foreign periods; pension amount still depends on actual Canadian residence. Current official agency guidance independently checked for this material claim.
question: Si je vis à l’étranger, quelle durée de résidence au Canada faut-il normalement pour être admissible à la pension de la Sécurité de la vieillesse?
reference_answer: En règle générale, une personne qui réside à l'étranger et souhaite toucher la Sécurité de la vieillesse doit avoir résidé au Canada pendant au moins 20 ans après l'âge de 18 ans. Les conditions comprennent aussi le fait d'avoir au moins 65 ans et d'avoir été citoyen canadien ou résident légal avant de quitter le Canada. Une entente internationale de sécurité sociale peut permettre de totaliser certaines périodes étrangères pour déterminer l'admissibilité.

context_text: Eligible newcomers can apply for certain CRA benefit and credit payments before filing their first Canadian tax return. For eligible Canada child benefit applications CRA points to Form RC66; personal status, arrival and income information may be needed. Current official agency guidance independently checked for this material claim.
question: Can a newcomer apply for CRA benefit and credit payments before filing a first Canadian tax return?
reference_answer: Yes, if eligible. A newcomer who becomes a Canadian tax resident may apply for certain CRA benefits and credits before filing a first Canadian tax return. The required forms depend on the benefit—for example an eligible family's Canada child benefit application may use form RC66 and supporting information about arrival, status and previous income. Filing subsequent tax returns is still important to maintain benefit eligibility and amounts.

context_text: The Canada Disability Savings Bond can be paid into an eligible RDSP without any personal contribution. Unlike the bond, the Canada Disability Savings Grant is a matching payment linked to eligible contributions; benefits depend on qualifying criteria and income. Current official agency guidance independently checked for this material claim.
question: Dans un REEI, dois-je cotiser pour recevoir le Bon canadien pour l’épargne-invalidité?
reference_answer: Non. Le Bon canadien pour l'épargne-invalidité peut être versé dans un régime enregistré d'épargne-invalidité (REEI) sans cotisation personnelle si les conditions de revenu et d'admissibilité sont réunies. La Subvention canadienne pour l'épargne-invalidité est différente : elle est généralement versée en contrepartie de cotisations admissibles au REEI. Les règles de rétroactivité et les plafonds annuels et à vie peuvent s'appliquer.

context_text: FHSA participation room is $8,000 in the calendar year the individual's first FHSA is opened; earlier unopened years do not accrue room. Later-year unused-room carryforward is permitted subject to statutory limits and the $40,000 lifetime cap. Current official agency guidance independently checked for this material claim.
question: Can I build up unused FHSA participation room in years before I open my first FHSA?
