reference_answer: No. Your first-home savings account (FHSA) participation room begins in the calendar year when you open your first FHSA, normally with $8,000 of room in that year. You do not accumulate FHSA room in earlier years before opening an account. After opening, eligible unused room can carry forward up to the statutory annual carryforward limit, subject to the $40,000 lifetime contribution limit and other conditions.

context_text: A separation caused by relationship breakdown requires at least 90 consecutive days apart before CRA recognizes the separated status. After the qualifying period, the effective date is the first day apart; separation due solely to work or health is not equivalent. Current official agency guidance independently checked for this material claim.
question: My partner and I separated because our relationship broke down. Do I report myself as separated to CRA after just one month apart?
reference_answer: No. CRA does not treat a breakdown-related separation as reportable after only one month apart. You must have lived apart for at least 90 consecutive days for that reason. After 90 days, report the change with the effective date being when you first began living apart. Separation for work or health is not equivalent.

context_text: Government of Canada cheques, including CRA cheques, do not expire and can ordinarily be cashed years later. If a cheque is lost, stolen or damaged, CRA provides a process to identify the payment and request a replacement. Current official agency guidance independently checked for this material claim.
question: J’ai retrouvé un vieux chèque de l’ARC. Est-il périmé parce qu’il date de plusieurs années?
reference_answer: Non. Les chèques du gouvernement du Canada, y compris ceux de l'ARC, n'expirent pas. Un ancien chèque peut généralement être encaissé même après plusieurs années. Si le chèque est perdu, volé, endommagé ou impossible à encaisser, communiquez avec l'ARC pour demander un remplacement.

context_text: An eTA is electronically linked to the passport used in its application, and a newly issued passport requires a new eTA. Canadian citizens and Canadian permanent residents cannot apply for an eTA; its application rules concern eligible foreign nationals. Direct current issuer guidance checked for the specified facts.
question: I renewed my passport. Can I still fly to Canada using the eTA linked to my old passport?
reference_answer: No. If you are a foreign national who requires an electronic travel authorization (eTA) to fly to Canada, an eTA linked to an old passport is not valid with your newly issued passport. Apply for a new eTA using your new passport. Canadian citizens and permanent residents cannot apply for an eTA, so this rule is relevant only where an eTA is required.

context_text: A Canadian study permit is not itself a visa or travel document and does not guarantee admission. Re-entry depends on a valid passport and, where required, a valid TRV or eTA, plus meeting border admissibility requirements. Direct current issuer guidance checked for the specified facts.
question: Est-ce qu’un permis d’études canadien remplace un visa de visiteur pour entrer au Canada?
reference_answer: Non. Le permis d'études permet d'étudier au Canada, mais n'est pas un document de voyage et ne garantit pas l'entrée. Selon la nationalité et le moyen de transport, il faut parfois aussi un visa de résident temporaire ou une autorisation de voyage électronique (AVE), en plus du passeport applicable. Un agent frontalier vérifie l'admissibilité.

context_text: New Brunswick Horizon and Vitalité regional health authorities both provide patient services in English and French. Section 19 provides Vitalité operates administratively in French, Horizon in English, while both serve members of public in their chosen official language. Direct current issuer guidance checked for the specified facts.
question: Do both Horizon and Vitalité provide services in English and French in New Brunswick?
reference_answer: Yes. New Brunswick's two regional health authorities, Horizon and Vitalité, provide health services in English and French. Under the Regional Health Authorities Act, Vitalité operates administratively in French and Horizon in English, but both must serve patients in their choice of official language. This does not mean every individual clinician is personally bilingual.

context_text: An institution appearing as a DLI does not mean all its individual programs qualify for a PGWP. Students must satisfy program-specific and other PGWP criteria, including applicable language and field-of-study rules. Direct current issuer guidance checked for the specified facts.
question: Does finding a college on Canada’s designated learning institutions list mean every program there qualifies for a PGWP?
reference_answer: No. A designated learning institution (DLI) is authorized to host international students, but not all programs at a DLI qualify graduates for a post-graduation work permit (PGWP). Check the specific program, field-of-study and language requirements where applicable, and all the student's other eligibility conditions.

context_text: IRCC determines the child biometrics age exemption using age on the date the application was submitted. An applicant who was 13 when applying remains exempt on that application despite turning 14 while it is processed. Direct current issuer guidance checked for the specified facts.
question: Mon enfant avait 13 ans au dépôt de sa demande et a maintenant 14 ans. Doit-il fournir ses données biométriques uniquement parce qu’il a eu son anniversaire?
reference_answer: Non. IRCC évalue l'âge au moment où la demande est présentée. Si votre enfant avait 13 ans ou moins au dépôt de la demande, l'exemption de collecte biométrique continue de s'appliquer à cette demande, même s'il fête ses 14 ans avant que le dossier soit traité.

context_text: A stolen Canadian passport outside Canada should be reported to the nearest Canadian government office abroad. Once reported as stolen, the passport is cancelled and can no longer be used for travel; replacement procedures apply. Direct current issuer guidance checked for the specified facts.
question: My Canadian passport was stolen while I was abroad. Which Canadian office should I contact first?
reference_answer: Contact the nearest Government of Canada office abroad, such as the Canadian embassy, consulate or high commission, as soon as possible to report your stolen passport. Officials can explain replacement or emergency travel-document options. A reported stolen passport is cancelled; local police reporting may also be appropriate depending on local requirements.

context_text: Citizenship test normally applies to applicants age 18 to 54 on the date they sign their Canadian citizenship application. An applicant who signed at age 54 and turns 55 before the test remains subject to the test absent an applicable waiver or exemption. Direct current issuer guidance checked for the specified facts.
question: J’avais 54 ans quand j’ai signé ma demande de citoyenneté et j’en ai maintenant 55. Quel âge compte pour l’examen?
reference_answer: L'âge au moment de la signature de votre demande de citoyenneté canadienne est celui qui compte. Si vous aviez 54 ans le jour où vous avez signé, vous devez normalement passer l'examen même si vous avez maintenant 55 ans. L'examen est habituellement exigé pour les personnes âgées de 18 à 54 ans inclusivement à la signature, sauf exemption particulière.

context_text: When a planning district adopted district-wide zoning under s.69, variance application goes to the planning district board. Otherwise the applicant applies to the council of the municipality containing the affected property. Direct issuer source reviewed for the asserted requirement.
question: Au Manitoba, à qui dois-je présenter une demande de dérogation si le district d’aménagement a adopté un règlement de zonage pour tout le district?
reference_answer: Au Manitoba, si un district d'aménagement a adopté un règlement de zonage applicable à tout le district en vertu de l'article 69 de la Loi sur l'aménagement du territoire, présentez la demande de dérogation à la commission de ce district. Dans les autres cas, présentez-la au conseil de la municipalité où se trouve le bien. Une délégation des décisions est possible si les conditions de la loi et des règlements le permettent.

context_text: Federal Ombudsperson deals exclusively with federal-jurisdiction matters such as federal victims services and federal corrections-related complaints. The office does not oversee provincial justice administration, though it may refer people to appropriate provincial services. Direct issuer source reviewed for the asserted requirement.
question: Is the federal ombudsperson for victims of crime responsible for every issue a victim might have with the justice system?
reference_answer: No. The Office of the Federal Ombudsperson for Victims of Crime deals with matters within federal jurisdiction, such as access to federal victim services and complaints relating to federally regulated corrections or parole. It cannot intervene in every provincial or territorial police, prosecution or court matter; for those, a provincial or territorial complaints body may be appropriate.

context_text: The Correctional Investigator has independent oversight of people in Correctional Service of Canada's custody or supervision. Mandate concerns federal corrections and does not ordinarily extend to provincially managed jails or prisons. Direct issuer source reviewed for the asserted requirement.
question: Le Bureau de l’enquêteur correctionnel du Canada peut-il enquêter sur les établissements correctionnels provinciaux, ou son mandat porte-t-il seulement sur le système fédéral?
reference_answer: Non. Le Bureau de l'enquêteur correctionnel est un ombudsman indépendant chargé de surveiller le traitement des personnes sous la garde ou la surveillance du Service correctionnel du Canada, c'est-à-dire relevant du système correctionnel fédéral. Il ne surveille pas automatiquement les prisons provinciales ou les personnes dont la peine est administrée par une province.

context_text: A Canadian record suspension separates an eligible conviction record from normal CPIC search results; it does not erase the conviction. Suspensions may be revoked and may be identified in particular vulnerable-sector searches; foreign entry is not guaranteed. Direct issuer source reviewed for the asserted requirement.
question: Does a Canadian record suspension erase the conviction from my record entirely?
reference_answer: No. A Canadian record suspension sets eligible federal conviction records apart from ordinary criminal records, and generally removes them from standard CPIC search results. It does not erase the fact of conviction, guarantee entry to another country or permanently protect against revocation. Certain vulnerable-sector checks can still reveal relevant record information under statutory conditions.

context_text: Section 32 applies to federal Parliament and federal government, and to each provincial legislature and government in its area of authority. Charter ordinarily binds government conduct rather than all interactions between private parties. Direct issuer source reviewed for the asserted requirement.
question: La Charte canadienne s’applique-t-elle au gouvernement provincial ou seulement au gouvernement fédéral?
reference_answer: Elle s'applique aux deux ordres de gouvernement. Le paragraphe 32(1) de la Charte canadienne des droits et libertés vise le Parlement et le gouvernement du Canada dans leurs domaines de compétence, mais aussi la législature et le gouvernement de chacune des provinces dans leurs domaines. Cela ne veut pas dire que la Charte s'applique automatiquement de la même manière à toutes les relations purement privées.

context_text: An individual can complain first to the relevant Saskatchewan health trustee about alleged improper use or disclosure of protected personal health information. Saskatchewan Information and Privacy Commissioner accepts qualifying HIPA privacy complaints and reviews after the affected trustee's response. Direct issuer source reviewed for the asserted requirement.
question: En Saskatchewan, à qui puis-je signaler une atteinte présumée à la confidentialité de mes renseignements personnels de santé?
reference_answer: Vous pouvez d'abord signaler une utilisation ou une communication présumée abusive de vos renseignements personnels de santé au dépositaire concerné, comme un établissement ou un professionnel de santé. Vous pouvez aussi déposer une plainte auprès du Commissariat à l'information et à la protection de la vie privée de la Saskatchewan, qui examine les problèmes couverts par la Health Information Protection Act. Les démarches et recours dépendent de la nature du dossier.

context_text: A notwithstanding declaration ceases to operate after five years or an earlier deadline in the Act. Parliament or a legislature may re-enact a declaration, but each renewal is itself limited to five years. Direct issuer source reviewed for the asserted requirement.
question: Can a notwithstanding-clause declaration remain in force indefinitely without renewal?
reference_answer: No. Under section 33(3) of the Canadian Charter, a notwithstanding declaration expires after five years or an earlier date specified in the law. Parliament or the provincial legislature may re-enact the declaration, but each re-enactment is subject to the same five-year maximum. The declaration cannot simply remain effective forever without renewal.

context_text: Incorporation by reference makes all or part of an external standard legally binding without reproducing its contents in the regulation. The incorporated edition may be static or ambulatory; the correct identified version governs compliance. Direct issuer source reviewed for the asserted requirement.
question: Quand un règlement fédéral incorpore une norme par renvoi, faut-il nécessairement reproduire cette norme dans le règlement?
reference_answer: Non. L'incorporation par renvoi permet d'intégrer tout ou partie d'un document ou d'une norme au régime d'un règlement sans en reproduire intégralement le texte. Le contenu incorporé peut avoir force obligatoire; pour interpréter les exigences applicables, il faut donc identifier la norme exacte et, selon les règles du renvoi, la version pertinente.

context_text: The federal confidence convention applies to ministries formed from a majority or minority of House of Commons seats. Loss on a clear confidence question ordinarily leads a ministry to resign or seek dissolution; minority governments are more exposed to such losses. Issuer text supports these specified material facts.
question: Does the confidence convention apply only to minority governments in Canada?
reference_answer: No. Canada's confidence convention applies to both majority and minority governments. The Prime Minister and Cabinet must retain the confidence of the House of Commons to govern, regardless of how many seats the governing party holds. Defeat on a clear confidence question normally leads the government to resign or seek dissolution; minority governments are simply more vulnerable to such defeats.

context_text: The prefix S denotes a bill first introduced in the Senate, while prefix C denotes introduction in the House of Commons. Senate bills include both government bills and bills from individual senators, so S alone does not identify its sponsor or government status. Issuer text supports these specified material facts.
question: Dans LEGISinfo, le préfixe S suffit-il pour savoir qu’un projet de loi est une initiative du gouvernement?
reference_answer: Non. Dans LEGISinfo, la lettre S indique que le projet de loi a été déposé au Sénat; elle ne révèle pas à elle seule s'il s'agit d'une initiative gouvernementale. Des projets de loi du gouvernement et des projets de loi de sénateurs individuels peuvent porter le préfixe S. Il faut consulter la catégorie et le parrain du projet plutôt que déduire son type du seul préfixe.

context_text: The Alberta Human Rights Act applies to protected-ground discrimination in rental advertisements, applications, tenancy terms and treatment. Landlords must provide reasonable accommodation in rental housing up to undue hardship, with exceptions under law. Issuer text supports these specified material facts.
question: Does Alberta’s human rights law cover discrimination when someone is trying to rent a place to live?
reference_answer: Yes. Alberta's Human Rights Act prohibits discrimination on protected grounds when someone applies to rent housing and during a tenancy, including advertising, applicant selection and lease terms. A landlord must also consider reasonable accommodation to the point of undue hardship, subject to relevant legal exceptions.

context_text: Both French and English versions of federal legal texts covered by section 13 are enacted or published simultaneously and are equally authoritative. Neither official-language version is automatically inferior; interpreting both is required where wording diverges. Issuer text supports these specified material facts.
question: La version française d’une loi fédérale fait-elle autant autorité que la version anglaise?
reference_answer: Oui. Pour les textes visés à l'article 13 de la Loi sur les langues officielles, les versions française et anglaise sont simultanées et font également autorité. Une version n'est pas automatiquement une simple traduction juridiquement inférieure à l'autre. En cas de divergence, il faut interpréter les deux versions selon les principes d'interprétation bilingue.

context_text: The Indigenous Languages Act establishes the Office to support First Nations, Inuit and Métis efforts to reclaim and revitalize Indigenous languages. The office supports Indigenous-led language priorities, public awareness and innovation rather than replacing community language governance. Issuer text supports these specified material facts.
question: What does the Office of the Commissioner of Indigenous Languages do to support language revitalization?
reference_answer: The Office of the Commissioner of Indigenous Languages supports First Nations, Inuit and Métis efforts to reclaim, revitalize, maintain and strengthen Indigenous languages. It promotes recognition of language rights, encourages innovative methods and technologies, and works with Indigenous governments and organizations; it does not replace the authority of the language communities themselves.

context_text: Indian Act section 87 exempts specified personal property of a registered Indian or band situated on reserve, not every asset anywhere. The provision is subject to section 83 and section 5 of First Nations Fiscal Management Act and can require determining a property's location. Issuer text supports these specified material facts.
question: L’article 87 de la Loi sur les Indiens exonère-t-il tous les biens meubles d’un membre inscrit d’une Première Nation?
reference_answer: Non. L'alinéa 87(1)b) de la Loi sur les Indiens protège de l'impôt certains biens meubles d'un « Indien » ou d'une bande, mais seulement lorsqu'ils sont situés sur une réserve au sens applicable. L'article 87 est aussi soumis aux exceptions mentionnées dans sa formulation. La détermination du lieu d'un bien ou d'un revenu nécessite parfois un examen des liens avec la réserve et d'autres dispositions légales.

context_text: The First Nations FMS certificate follows review of a Nation's implementation of its approved Financial Administration Law and governance practices. The FMB uses independent document review, staff interviews and on-site testing; it is not a guarantee no future financial issues occur. Issuer text supports these specified material facts.
question: What does a Financial Management System certificate from the First Nations Financial Management Board say about a First Nation’s administration?
reference_answer: A Financial Management System certificate from the First Nations Financial Management Board confirms that a First Nation has demonstrated, through an independent assessment, that it implements its approved Financial Administration Law and follows the specified financial and administrative governance practices. It is not a general political rating or a guarantee that no financial problem could ever occur.

context_text: BC's Personal Information Protection Act protects information handled by private organizations including incorporated non-profit societies. Private-sector privacy rights encompass access and use/disclosure limits, subject to statutory conditions. Issuer text supports these specified material facts.
question: En Colombie-Britannique, la loi provinciale sur les renseignements personnels du secteur privé peut-elle aussi viser un organisme sans but lucratif?
reference_answer: Oui. En Colombie-Britannique, la Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) encadre les pratiques de protection des renseignements personnels d'organisations privées, y compris des organismes sans but lucratif, des organismes de bienfaisance et des sociétés commerciales. Les exigences concrètes dépendent des données recueillies et des activités, et le commissaire provincial peut recevoir des plaintes relevant de la loi.

context_text: Treaty annuity eligibility requires registration under the Indian Act and affiliation with a First Nation under a qualifying historic treaty. Registration alone is insufficient without the specific treaty relationship, and annuity amounts depend on treaty provisions. Issuer text supports these specified material facts.
question: Does registration under the Indian Act by itself make someone eligible for an annual treaty annuity?
reference_answer: No. Registration under the Indian Act is one eligibility element, but treaty annuity payments also require affiliation with a First Nation that signed a historic treaty with the Crown that provides for annuity payments. Registration alone, without the required treaty affiliation, does not establish eligibility. Payment amounts and procedures depend on the particular treaty.

context_text: In the ordinary Indian Act regime a band council's reserve land allotment requires ministerial approval for lawful possession. A Certificate of Possession may then evidence the right, and the rule should not be assumed for First Nations operating under separate land codes. Issuer text supports these specified material facts.
question: Sous le régime de la Loi sur les Indiens, une attribution de possession par le conseil de bande suffit-elle à elle seule pour détenir légalement une parcelle de réserve?
reference_answer: Non. Dans le régime ordinaire de l'article 20(1) de la Loi sur les Indiens, l'attribution de la possession d'une parcelle de réserve par le conseil de bande ne suffit pas : l'approbation du ministre est aussi requise. Un certificat de possession peut ensuite constater le droit; l'article 20 prévoit également des mécanismes d'occupation temporaire. Cette règle n'est pas à transposer automatiquement aux Premières Nations ayant adopté leur propre code foncier.

context_text: Equal per-capita CHT sets funding by the number of residents rather than giving each province an identical total amount. A province with greater population normally receives more in gross CHT funds; Canada Health Act deductions are a separate matter.
question: Does an equal per-capita Canada Health Transfer mean that every province receives the same total dollar amount?
reference_answer: No. Equal per-capita allocation means the Canada Health Transfer provides a comparable amount per person under the federal allocation formula, not an identical total transfer to each province. A more populous province generally receives a larger gross total than a less populous one, while the federal Canada Health Act conditions and possible deductions apply separately.

context_text: TFF is an annual unconditional transfer to Yukon, Northwest Territories and Nunavut for comparable public services. Territory-specific grants use assessed expenditure needs minus fiscal revenue capacity and recognize northern service costs.
question: À quoi sert la formule de financement des territoires et ce transfert fédéral est-il conditionnel?
reference_answer: La formule de financement des territoires est un transfert fédéral annuel inconditionnel versé au Yukon, aux Territoires du Nord-Ouest et au Nunavut. Elle tient compte de leurs besoins de dépenses et de leur capacité de générer des recettes pour les aider à financer des services publics comparables à ceux des provinces à des niveaux d'imposition comparables. Elle reflète notamment le coût élevé de services dans les collectivités nordiques isolées.

context_text: Yukon Government's agreements page names 14 treaties applying in Yukon, including 11 First Nations Final Agreements paired with self-government agreements. It also lists the Inuvialuit, Gwich'in and historical Treaty 11 arrangements; individual texts govern specific legal rights.
question: Where can I find the Yukon government’s list of treaties and self-government agreements with Indigenous governments?
reference_answer: Use the Government of Yukon's 'Find agreements with Indigenous governments and groups' page. It lists 14 treaties applying in the Yukon, including 11 Yukon First Nations Final Agreements paired with Self-Government Agreements, as well as transboundary agreements. The individual agreements set out rights, institutions and authorities, so consult the agreement for the specific government you are researching.

context_text: Canada's international social security agreements may combine CPP contributory periods with foreign qualifying periods to establish eligibility. Payment amounts depend on actual CPP contributions rather than automatically adding foreign earnings to Canadian contributions.
question: Can a social security agreement help me qualify for a Canadian pension if I spent part of my working life abroad?
reference_answer: Yes, depending on the agreement and the benefit. A Canadian social security agreement with another country may let you combine qualifying contribution or residence periods under both countries' systems to meet a minimum eligibility threshold for CPP or another covered pension. The Canadian CPP pension amount itself is generally calculated from your actual CPP contributions, not by treating all foreign contributions as Canadian earnings.

context_text: Following an absence of at least 48 hours, a returning Canadian resident can ordinarily claim up to CAD $800 in personal exemptions. For the 48-hour category, goods must be present and declared on re-entry; the seven-day category has different unaccompanied-goods rules.
question: Après 48 heures à l’étranger, quelle exemption personnelle s’applique normalement et les achats doivent-ils être avec moi au retour?
reference_answer: Après une absence d'au moins 48 heures à l'étranger, l'exemption personnelle ordinaire permet de rapporter jusqu'à 800 $ CA de marchandises sans droits ni taxes, sous réserve des conditions et des limites pour certains produits. Pour l'exemption de 48 heures, les biens doivent être en votre possession et déclarés au retour. Les règles sont différentes après une absence d'au moins sept jours, où certains biens peuvent suivre séparément.

context_text: Cannabis oils including THC or CBD generally cannot cross Canada's international border without Health Canada authorization. Domestic legal purchase or possession does not confer import/export permission; limited permits/exemptions are possible.
question: Can I bring cannabis oil across the Canadian border just because it was bought legally in Canada?
reference_answer: No. Buying cannabis oil legally in Canada does not allow you to take it across an international border. Canadian law generally prohibits importing or exporting cannabis, including oils containing THC or CBD, without a specific Health Canada permit or exemption. Legal possession within Canada and authorization to cross the border are different matters.

context_text: Export Development Canada is Canada's export credit agency and a federally owned Crown corporation supporting trade. It supplies financing and insurance and other export risk/market support to Canadian international businesses.
question: Quel rôle joue Exportation et développement Canada pour les entreprises qui font du commerce international?
reference_answer: Exportation et développement Canada (EDC) est l'organisme canadien de crédit à l'exportation et une société d'État fédérale. Il aide les entreprises canadiennes à développer leurs activités sur les marchés internationaux, notamment en offrant des solutions de financement, d'assurance-crédit, de garanties et de gestion des risques liés au commerce extérieur.

context_text: Nunavut's Office of the Languages Commissioner defines Inuktut as including Inuktitut and Inuinnaqtun. The umbrella term names recognized linguistic forms, without asserting the absence of internal dialectal variation.
question: Au Nunavut, quelles deux variétés le commissariat aux langues désigne-t-il par « inuktut » dans son explication des droits linguistiques?
reference_answer: Au Nunavut, le terme « inuktut » est employé par le Commissariat aux langues pour englober deux variétés de langue inuite reconnues dans le territoire : l'inuktitut et l'inuinnaqtun. Cette terminologie ne signifie pas qu'il n'existe aucune diversité dialectale dans ces variétés; elle précise la portée du terme utilisé dans le régime territorial.

context_text: Parks Canada explicitly says campsite reservation fees do not necessarily include national park entrance fees. Visitors need valid admission when entry fees apply; free-admission windows such as summer 2026 don't turn a reservation into an admission pass.
question: When reserving a campsite with Parks Canada, does the reservation automatically give me a national park admission pass?
reference_answer: No. A Parks Canada campsite reservation is separate from park admission. If admission fees apply, you must obtain an applicable park admission pass or pay the required daily admission in addition to reservation/camping fees, unless a particular fee exemption applies. A Discovery Pass is one option for admission, not automatically provided with the booking.

context_text: Federal reprisal complaint ordinary time limit is 60 days from known/ought-to-have-known date. Commissioner may grant extension depending on circumstances; policy revised October 8 2026.
question: Dans le régime fédéral de protection des divulgateurs, à partir de quand calcule-t-on le délai pour porter plainte pour représailles?
reference_answer: Le délai ordinaire pour déposer une plainte de représailles auprès du Commissariat à l'intégrité du secteur public du Canada est de 60 jours à partir du jour où la personne savait, ou aurait dû savoir, qu'une mesure de représailles avait été prise. Le commissaire peut proroger ce délai selon les circonstances. La politique du 8 octobre 2026 précise que le simple fait de découvrir tardivement la loi ne suffit pas nécessairement à justifier une prolongation.

context_text: An eligible account holder can view and print their Social Insurance Number from MSCA. The dashboard also shows recorded names and any SIN expiry date; SIN remains sensitive personal information.
question: Can I view and print my SIN through My Service Canada Account?
reference_answer: Yes. In My Service Canada Account, you can view and print your Social Insurance Number and check your name as recorded and any expiry date. Register or sign in, then open the 'Social Insurance Number' section. Your SIN is sensitive personal information, so protect copies and don't provide it when unnecessary.

context_text: Non-residents may withdraw TFSA funds free of Canadian tax, with withdrawn amount normally restored as contribution room on January 1 of next year. A TFSA contribution made while non-resident is generally subject to 1% monthly tax, even where unused contribution room is available; exception for qualifying transfers.
question: Si je retire de l’argent de mon CELI pendant que je suis non-résident, puis-je recotiser en franchise d’impôt sans redevenir résident?
reference_answer: Non. Un non-résident du Canada peut retirer de l'argent de son CELI sans impôt canadien sur le retrait, et ce retrait crée normalement des droits de cotisation à compter du 1er janvier suivant. Cependant, une cotisation effectuée alors que la personne est non-résidente est imposable, généralement à 1 % par mois tant qu'elle demeure dans le compte, même s'il existe des droits inutilisés. Il faut attendre d'être redevenu résident pour cotiser à nouveau en franchise d'impôt.

context_text: NWT property assessment assigns land/building value and is distinct from the property-tax notice. NWT taxes generally use assessed value × mill rate / 1000; municipal tax communities and general taxation areas have different taxing authorities.
question: What is the difference between a property assessment and a property tax bill in the Northwest Territories?
reference_answer: A property assessment in the Northwest Territories assigns a taxable value to a property; it is not the bill itself. The relevant taxing authority applies a tax rate or mill rate and applicable adjustments to the assessed value to determine the taxes owed. NWT Municipal and Community Affairs handles assessments, while municipal or territorial authorities administer taxation depending on location.

context_text: The party offering an electronic document as evidence bears burden of establishing authenticity. The burden requires evidence capable of supporting finding that document is what proponent asserts; best evidence is separate question.
question: Who has to show that an electronic document is authentic when it’s offered as evidence under the Canada Evidence Act?
reference_answer: The party seeking to admit the electronic document as evidence must prove its authenticity, by offering evidence capable of supporting a finding that the document is what the party claims it to be. Section 31.1 of the Canada Evidence Act places that burden on the proponent; this authentication requirement is distinct from the Act's separate best-evidence rule for electronic records.

context_text: Under s9(1)(a), a renouncing Canadian must already possess another country's citizenship or become one upon acceptance. Humanitarian ministerial discretion in s9(2) waives only s9(1)(d) or (e); it cannot waive other nationality requirement (a).
question: Puis-je renoncer à ma citoyenneté canadienne si cela me rend apatride?
reference_answer: Non, pas selon la procédure ordinaire de renonciation prévue à l'article 9 de la Loi sur la citoyenneté. Vous devez déjà posséder une autre nationalité ou l'acquérir si votre demande est acceptée, afin de ne pas devenir apatride par cette renonciation. Le ministre peut dispenser de certaines autres conditions pour motifs d'ordre humanitaire, mais cette dispense ne s'étend pas à l'exigence d'une autre nationalité.

context_text: One eligible elector can ordinarily vouch for identity/address of only one other elector per election. An eligible employee of seniors residence or long-term care facility can vouch for more than one resident under special conditions.
question: Can I vouch for several neighbours who lack ID in a federal election?
reference_answer: Generally no. Under the Canada Elections Act, a voter may normally vouch for the identity and address of only one other person in a federal election. There are limited exceptions, such as qualified employees assisting residents of seniors' residences or long-term care facilities, subject to specific rules. A person cannot vouch for several neighbours merely because they know them.

context_text: ATI Act s19(1) generally requires refusing disclosure of an individual's personal information. Subsection 19(2) permits disclosure with consent, public availability or consistency with Privacy Act s8; exemptions are fact-specific.
question: Un ministère fédéral doit-il toujours refuser de communiquer des renseignements personnels dans une réponse d’accès à l’information?
reference_answer: Non. L'article 19(1) de la Loi sur l'accès à l'information exige en principe de refuser la divulgation des renseignements personnels. Toutefois, le paragraphe 19(2) autorise une communication si la personne concernée consent, si les renseignements sont déjà accessibles au public ou si l'article 8 de la Loi sur la protection des renseignements personnels le permet. Il faut vérifier que l'une de ces exceptions s'applique réellement.

context_text: Ontario IPC hears appeals of municipal and provincial access-to-information decisions, including refusal or fee disputes. For requests after July 1 2026 Ontario institutions generally have 45 business days, and appeal deadlines use 30 business days; earlier requests follow old regime.
question: Who hears an appeal if an Ontario municipality refuses my request for municipal records?
reference_answer: The Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario (IPC) independently handles appeals from access decisions made by municipalities and other bodies covered by the Municipal Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act. Check the decision letter for appeal instructions and deadline; the IPC first reviews jurisdiction and may use mediation or adjudication.

context_text: After six consecutive months of employment, federally regulated employee may request change to work location, schedule or hours. Request must be written with information in s177.1; employer may refuse based on specified statutory grounds, so change is not automatic.
question: Après six mois de travail continu dans un emploi assujetti au régime fédéral, puis-je demander un changement de lieu de travail?
reference_answer: Oui. Après six mois consécutifs de service continu auprès d'un employeur de compétence fédérale, vous pouvez demander par écrit une modification de votre lieu de travail en vertu de l'article 177.1 du Code canadien du travail. La demande doit préciser notamment la modification et les dates souhaitées. L'employeur doit y répondre suivant le Code, mais il peut refuser pour certains motifs légaux; le droit de demander n'est pas une garantie d'obtenir le changement.

context_text: When both French and English chosen by federal-court parties, judge or other hearing officer must understand both without interpreter. The bilingual-competence duty applies to adjudicative functions and is not equivalent to banning all court interpretation services.
question: If both official languages are chosen by the parties in a federal court proceeding, can the judge rely on an interpreter to understand one of them?
reference_answer: No, not for understanding the evidence and arguments in the chosen official languages. Under section 16(1)(c) of the federal Official Languages Act, if the parties choose both English and French in proceedings before a federal court, the court must ensure that every judge or other officer hearing the case understands both languages without an interpreter. The requirement concerns the court's adjudicative functions, not every employee or every courtroom service.

context_text: Ordinary application for review of federal board/tribunal decision due within 30 days after decision first communicated. Federal Court can permit extension, and other statutes may set special shorter or longer periods.
question: Quel délai ordinaire la Loi sur les Cours fédérales fixe-t-elle pour demander le contrôle judiciaire d’une décision d’un office fédéral?
reference_answer: En règle générale, l'article 18.1(2) de la Loi sur les Cours fédérales fixe un délai de 30 jours après la première communication de la décision d'un office fédéral à la partie directement touchée pour déposer une demande de contrôle judiciaire. La Cour fédérale peut autoriser un délai supplémentaire, avant ou après l'échéance. Certaines lois particulières, notamment en immigration, imposent toutefois des délais différents.

context_text: Board of directors manages or supervises management of federally incorporated company's business and affairs. The management duty is explicitly subject to unanimous shareholders' agreement, which can restrict director powers.
question: Who is responsible for managing a federally incorporated business corporation’s affairs?
reference_answer: Under section 102(1) of the Canada Business Corporations Act, the board of directors manages or supervises management of the business and affairs of a federally incorporated business corporation. A unanimous shareholder agreement may restrict the directors' authority and transfer specified decision-making powers. The directors' governance role should not be confused with management's day-to-day operations.

context_text: Québec small-claims filing fee differs between natural and legal persons. 2026 filing fee on a claim no higher than $5,000 is $121 natural person, $191 legal person.
question: Au Québec, les frais de dépôt aux petites créances sont-ils les mêmes pour un particulier et une société?
reference_answer: Non. Le tarif québécois de dépôt d'une demande aux petites créances distingue les personnes physiques des personnes morales, et varie également selon le montant réclamé. Par exemple, selon le tarif en vigueur le 1er janvier 2026, une demande de 5 000 $ ou moins coûte 121 $ pour une personne physique et 191 $ pour une personne morale. Les tarifs sont indexés chaque année; consultez le tarif applicable à la date du dépôt.

context_text: Qualifying student debt ordinarily not discharged if bankruptcy occurs less than seven years after ceasing full- or part-time studies. Court can grant hardship relief from student-loan exception after five years if good faith and ongoing financial inability; not after three.
question: Can bankruptcy discharge a government student loan if I stopped being a student only three years ago?
reference_answer: Ordinarily no. Under section 178(1)(g) of the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act, a qualifying federal or provincial student loan is not discharged if bankruptcy occurs while the borrower is still a student or within seven years after they cease to be a full- or part-time student. After five years, a court may grant hardship relief if the borrower has acted in good faith and will continue to experience financial difficulty that prevents repayment. At three years, that hardship exception is not yet available.

context_text: Importers must send information in their control to Minister and original supplier within two days after awareness of reportable incident. When manufacturer outside Canada, importer must also file written report within ten days, unless Minister specifies another period.
question: En combien de temps un importateur doit-il transmettre les renseignements dont il dispose sur un incident lié à un produit de consommation?
reference_answer: En vertu de l'article 14(2) de la Loi canadienne sur la sécurité des produits de consommation, une personne qui importe un produit de consommation à des fins commerciales et qui prend connaissance d'un incident visé par la loi doit fournir au ministre et, le cas échéant, au fournisseur les renseignements en sa possession dans les deux jours suivant le jour où elle en prend connaissance. Si le fabricant est établi à l'extérieur du Canada, l'importateur doit en outre présenter au ministre le rapport écrit prévu au paragraphe 14(3) dans les dix jours suivant cette prise de connaissance, sauf délai différent précisé par le ministre.

context_text: Minister is responsible for administration and management of national parks. Ecological integrity, by protection of natural resources/processes, is the Minister's first priority for all park-management decisions.
question: What does the Canada National Parks Act say should come first when the minister manages a national park?
reference_answer: Maintaining or restoring ecological integrity is the first priority when the minister considers any aspect of managing Canada's national parks. Under section 8(2) of the Canada National Parks Act, this means putting protection of natural resources and natural processes first, while making park-use and visitor decisions within that framework. It does not make recreation or heritage education irrelevant; they must be considered consistently with that statutory priority.

context_text: A national emergency must be urgent, critical and temporary and meet danger to Canadians beyond a province's capacity/authority or serious sovereignty/security threat. In either case, it must be a situation not effectively addressable under any other Canadian law; provincial capacity alone is insufficient.
question: Une crise qui dépasse les capacités d’une province est-elle automatiquement une urgence nationale au sens de la Loi sur les mesures d’urgence?
reference_answer: Non. Le fait qu'une situation dépasse les capacités d'une province ne suffit pas, à lui seul, à satisfaire à la définition d'« urgence nationale » de l'article 3 de la Loi sur les mesures d'urgence. Il faut une situation temporaire, urgente et critique qui, soit menace gravement la vie, la santé ou la sécurité des Canadiens et dépasse les capacités ou compétences d'une province, soit menace gravement la souveraineté, la sécurité ou l'intégrité territoriale du Canada. Dans les deux cas, aucune autre loi fédérale ne doit permettre d'y faire face efficacement.

context_text: Manitoba ordinary eligible coverage persists for remainder of move month and next two months after permanent move. Exception: Manitoba temporary foreign worker coverage stops the day worker leaves Manitoba.
question: How long does Manitoba health coverage generally continue after I permanently move to another Canadian province?
reference_answer: When an ordinarily eligible Manitoba resident permanently moves to another province or territory, Manitoba health coverage generally continues for the rest of the month of arrival there and the following two months. Apply promptly to the new province's health plan to avoid a gap. Important exception: Manitoba says its coverage for a temporary foreign worker ends on the day the worker leaves Manitoba, so the general two-month extension should not be presented as universal.

context_text: A person offered employer dental insurance remains ineligible for CDCP even if they decline enrolment or must pay premium. Narrow exception exists for some retired pension-plan members who opted out before December 11 2023 and cannot rejoin; merely refusing employer plan is insufficient.
question: Si je refuse l’assurance dentaire offerte par mon employeur, est-ce que je peux répondre que je n’y ai pas accès pour le régime dentaire canadien?
reference_answer: En règle générale, non. Pour le Régime canadien de soins dentaires, le fait d'avoir accès à une assurance dentaire privée admissible offerte par votre employeur vous rend inadmissible, même si vous choisissez de ne pas vous y inscrire ou si vous devez payer une prime. La règle porte sur l'accès, pas seulement sur l'utilisation réelle de l'assurance. Une exception très précise concerne certaines personnes retraitées ayant renoncé à la couverture d'un régime de pension avant le 11 décembre 2023 et ne pouvant y revenir, mais ne s'applique pas simplement à un refus de l'assurance de l'employeur.

context_text: Disability Tax Credit is necessary but not sufficient for Canada Disability Benefit eligibility. 2026 rules also require age, residence, status, 2025 tax filing and other conditions.
question: Does being approved for the disability tax credit automatically make me eligible for the Canada Disability Benefit?
reference_answer: No. Disability Tax Credit approval is necessary but not sufficient to receive the Canada Disability Benefit. You must also normally be aged 18–64, be a Canadian resident for income-tax purposes, have an eligible citizenship or immigration status, and ensure that you and your spouse or partner, if applicable, filed the required federal tax returns. For payments based on the rules posted in September 2026, the government requires 2025 returns. Eligibility may also depend on incarceration status.

context_text: Canada Benefits Finder filters federal supports by life situation, age/audience, need and province or territory. Finder provides informational results and links to administering programs, not a final eligibility determination. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Quel outil fédéral puis-je utiliser pour repérer des prestations selon ma situation personnelle?
reference_answer: Le Chercheur de prestations du gouvernement du Canada, sur Canada.ca, aide à trouver les prestations et programmes fédéraux selon des critères comme l'âge, la situation familiale, le lieu de résidence et les besoins. Les résultats orientent vers des renseignements officiels, mais ne constituent pas une décision d'admissibilité. Vérifiez ensuite les conditions et la procédure de demande propres à chaque programme.

context_text: Each $1 withdrawn from RDSP can trigger $3 repayment of recent grant/bond funds up to holdback amount. Rules include conditions and exceptions, so exact repayment not universally $3 per dollar.
question: Could a withdrawal from my RDSP make me repay more in government grants or bonds than I actually withdraw?
reference_answer: Yes, for many withdrawals before age 60. Under the registered disability savings plan's proportional repayment rule, withdrawing $1 can require repaying $3 in recent Canada Disability Savings Grants and Bonds, up to the plan's assistance holdback amount. The rule has important exceptions and changes, including ordinary withdrawals in or after the year the beneficiary turns 60 and certain situations following loss of Disability Tax Credit eligibility. The exact repayment depends on the plan's recent grants and bonds.

context_text: New Brunswick permits transfer of a Service New Brunswick-held deposit to incoming tenant taking over lease. Tenant and landlord must sign Security Deposit Transfer Tenant to Tenant form and submit to Tenant and Landlord Relations Office; assignment alone is insufficient. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Au Nouveau-Brunswick, puis-je faire transférer mon dépôt de garantie au nouveau locataire qui reprend mon bail?
reference_answer: Oui, si vous cédez votre bail et que le dépôt de garantie est détenu à votre nom par Service Nouveau-Brunswick, vous pouvez demander son transfert au nouveau locataire. Vous devez remplir le formulaire « Security Deposit Transfer Tenant to Tenant » et le faire signer par vous-même et le locateur, puis le transmettre au Bureau des relations entre locataires et propriétaires. Le transfert n'est pas automatique du seul fait de la cession du bail.

context_text: Current-year federal tuition amount up to $5,000 less required own use may be transferred to an eligible parent/grandparent or spouse etc. Tuition credits carried forward from earlier years may be claimed by the student in future, but cannot later be transferred to another person. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Can I transfer unused federal tuition credits from earlier years to a parent this year?
reference_answer: No. For the federal tuition tax credit, you may transfer only an eligible unused amount from the current tax year to a parent, grandparent, spouse or other designated eligible person, subject to the usual $5,000 maximum before reducing it by the amount needed for your own tax. Federal tuition credits carried forward from earlier years cannot be transferred to another person later; they remain available for you to use under CRA rules.

context_text: Federal medical expenses can generally be claimed for an eligible 12-month consecutive period ending in the 2025 tax year, not just Jan–Dec. Amounts already claimed in prior return cannot be claimed again; only eligible nonreimbursed amounts count, with some exceptional rules. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Pour les frais médicaux de ma déclaration fédérale, la période doit-elle toujours aller de janvier à décembre?
reference_answer: Non. Pour les lignes fédérales 33099 et 33199 relatives aux frais médicaux, vous pouvez généralement choisir une période admissible de douze mois consécutifs qui se termine pendant l'année d'imposition, plutôt que l'année civile de janvier à décembre. Les frais ne doivent pas avoir déjà été demandés dans une déclaration antérieure, et certaines exceptions existent, notamment dans une déclaration finale d'une personne décédée.

context_text: A 2025 sale of principal residence must be reported even if full principal-residence exemption removes capital gains tax. CRA says sale must be reported on Schedule 3 and Form T2091(IND) for 2025 disposal of principal residence. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: I sold my home in 2025. Do I still report the sale to CRA if it was my principal residence the whole time?
reference_answer: Yes. If you sold your Canadian home in 2025, report the disposition to the CRA even if the property qualified as your principal residence for every year you owned it and the gain is fully exempt. The 2025 return generally requires reporting the sale on Schedule 3 and completing the applicable principal-residence designation using Form T2091(IND). Failure to designate and report can affect eligibility for the exemption.

context_text: Ordinary small supplier ceases status on the specific taxable supply that pushes sales above $30,000 in one calendar quarter. GST/HST must be charged starting with that threshold-crossing supply itself, with registration effective no later than supply date. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Si mon entreprise dépasse le seuil ordinaire de 30 000 $ de fournitures taxables dans un seul trimestre, à partir de quelle vente dois-je percevoir la TPS/TVH?
reference_answer: Dans le cas ordinaire d'une entreprise dont les fournitures taxables dépassent 30 000 $ au cours d'un seul trimestre civil, vous cessez d'être un petit fournisseur à compter de la fourniture qui fait franchir le seuil. Vous devez percevoir la TPS/TVH sur cette fourniture elle-même, et non seulement sur les ventes ultérieures. La date d'effet de votre inscription doit être au plus tard celle de cette fourniture. D'autres règles peuvent s'appliquer selon le type d'entreprise et les fournitures.

context_text: Commercial filming/photography for expected gain in Yukon territorial parks requires territorial park commercial film and photo permit. Yukon outlines distinct park application process and notes other permissions (e.g. camp, land use, heritage) may separately apply. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Do I need a Yukon territorial park permit to film commercially in one of its parks?
reference_answer: Yes. Yukon requires a territorial park permit for commercial filming or photography in its territorial parks. Apply through the Yukon territorial park permit service before filming, and follow applicable park conditions and any separate permits needed for activities such as drone operations or wildlife disturbance. A general admission or camping reservation is not the same as authorization to film commercially.

context_text: CRA normally treats a child's time split between 40% and 60% with two people as shared custody (45% qualifies). Each eligible shared-custody caregiver generally gets 50% of their independently computed full-custody CCB amount, not all to one. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: If my child lives with me 45% of the time, does CRA automatically treat me as the only person who can receive the Canada child benefit?
reference_answer: No. If your child lives with you about 45% of the time and with another individual for the remainder, the CRA would generally consider that shared custody for the Canada child benefit, because its usual range is 40%–60%. If both people qualify, each receives 50% of the benefit amount they would have received with full custody, calculated using their own adjusted family net income. CRA does not give one person the full amount merely because they have slightly more days.

context_text: Permanent residents must ordinarily accumulate 730 qualifying days in a five-year period, not necessarily consecutively. If PR granted less than five years ago, IRCC assesses whether 730 days can still be attained by fifth anniversary; qualifying time abroad can count. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Un résident permanent doit-il passer 730 jours consécutifs au Canada pour conserver son statut?
reference_answer: Non. L'obligation habituelle de résidence permanente exige au moins 730 jours admissibles au Canada sur la période pertinente de cinq ans, sans qu'ils soient consécutifs. Certaines périodes passées à l'étranger peuvent compter, par exemple dans des situations particulières d'emploi ou de séjour avec un citoyen canadien. Si vous êtes résident permanent depuis moins de cinq ans, on vérifie plutôt si vous pourrez atteindre 730 jours avant votre cinquième anniversaire de résidence permanente.

context_text: Applicants on or after June 22 2023 qualify for up to five years per entry; eligible earlier holders entering after that date may qualify. Entry and length remain subject to CBSA admission decisions or specific shorter date imposed; visa is not unconditional guaranteed residence. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Does a Canadian super visa guarantee that my parent can stay for five years on arrival?
reference_answer: No. A super visa may allow a parent or grandparent to stay up to five years per entry, but admission is still subject to border-officer examination and to the specific status conditions granted. Under IRCC rules applying to super visa holders entering on or after June 22, 2023, a five-year stay is normally available when the officer admits them and does not specify a shorter authorized period. A super visa is not an unconditional guarantee of admission or of permission to remain beyond the authorized date.

context_text: Submitting a PR application is not itself an open work permit; BOWP requires a separate application and eligible immigration stream. Eligibility commonly depends on PR completeness/AOR or other stage, immigration status and stream-specific criteria; some streams need approved-in-principle. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Le dépôt de ma demande de résidence permanente me donne-t-il automatiquement un permis de travail ouvert transitoire?
reference_answer: Non. Le simple dépôt d'une demande de résidence permanente ne donne pas automatiquement droit à un permis de travail ouvert transitoire. Il faut présenter une demande distincte de permis de travail ouvert transitoire (PTOT/BOWP) et satisfaire aux conditions du volet de résidence permanente concerné, notamment avoir atteint l'étape pertinente du dossier et posséder un statut ou une admissibilité au rétablissement autorisé. Une preuve de dépôt seule ne suffit pas toujours.

context_text: In designated Red Seal trades the national interprovincial examination tests competence under harmonized trade standards. Qualifying workers who meet trade certification requirements and pass exam receive Red Seal endorsement, aiding mobility but not replacing licences. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Aux Territoires du Nord-Ouest, à quoi sert l’examen interprovincial du Sceau rouge dans un métier désigné?
reference_answer: Aux Territoires du Nord-Ouest, l'examen interprovincial du Sceau rouge sert à vérifier qu'une personne qualifiée dans un métier désigné possède les compétences correspondant à la norme pancanadienne de ce métier. La réussite de l'examen, après satisfaction des autres exigences d'apprentissage ou de qualification, permet d'obtenir la mention Sceau rouge sur le certificat de qualification. La mention facilite la reconnaissance des compétences entre les provinces et territoires; elle ne remplace pas toutes les règles de licence propres à chaque métier.

context_text: Canadian returning to earlier passport name must submit a new passport application rather than just modifying or renewing existing document. Name-change evidence is needed; documents vary for relationship status, adoption or legal-name changes. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: Can I switch my Canadian passport back to my previous name without submitting a new application?
reference_answer: No. To return your name on a Canadian passport to a previous name, you generally must submit a new passport application with the supporting evidence of the name change. It is not done simply by editing the current passport or requesting an ordinary renewal. The precise documentation depends on whether the change follows a marriage, separation, divorce, adoption or legal name-change order.

context_text: Avoid non-essential travel is official government of Canada Travel Advice level 3, distinguishing significant risks. Level 4 Avoid all travel advises against any travel to the place, and regional advisories may differ from country-wide level. Matched stated fact to issuer's published guidance, scoped to relevant tax/program year.
question: « Évitez tout voyage non essentiel » est-il un véritable niveau d’avertissement du gouvernement canadien?
reference_answer: Oui. « Évitez tout voyage non essentiel » est l'un des quatre niveaux officiels des Conseils aux voyageurs et avertissements du gouvernement du Canada. C'est le niveau 3 : il signale des risques importants et conseille de ne voyager que si le déplacement est indispensable. Il est distinct du niveau 4, « Évitez tout voyage », qui déconseille de se rendre dans le pays ou la région pour quelque raison que ce soit. Un même pays peut aussi faire l'objet d'avertissements régionaux différents.

context_text: The consolidated sanctions list is for administrative purposes only, not itself a regulation with force of law. The 2026-09-22 list can lag regulatory amendments, so applicable regulations govern actual sanctions obligations.
question: Can I rely on Canada’s consolidated sanctions list as the actual legal text of a sanction?
reference_answer: No. The Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List is an administrative aid, not a regulation and not legally binding by itself. To determine whether a person, entity, transaction or activity is prohibited, consult the applicable sanctions regulation and any exemptions or permits. Global Affairs Canada warns that the consolidated list may lag behind new amendments; it also covers a defined subset of Canada's sanctions regimes.

context_text: Canadian consular officials can help detainees understand local procedures, access lawyers and contact family where permitted. Canadian consular officers cannot secure a prisoner's release, interfere with foreign law, or pay bail and defence costs.
question: Si je suis arrêté à l’étranger, le consulat canadien peut-il me faire sortir de prison?
reference_answer: Non. Si vous êtes arrêté ou détenu à l'étranger, les fonctionnaires consulaires canadiens peuvent expliquer les grandes lignes du système judiciaire local, vous fournir une liste d'avocats et chercher à communiquer avec vous ou à vérifier vos conditions de détention. Ils ne peuvent toutefois pas vous faire libérer, payer votre caution ou vos frais de défense, ni se substituer au tribunal ou à la police du pays concerné. Demandez aux autorités locales d'aviser le poste canadien le plus proche.

context_text: Nunavut's locally elected District Education Authorities work with Regional School Operations in hiring principals, teachers and school staff. Territorial Regional School Operations offices lead formal hiring, supervision and personnel management; DEA does not unilaterally hire all staff.
question: How do Nunavut’s district education authorities participate in hiring school staff?
reference_answer: Nunavut's District Education Authorities (DEAs) participate in hiring school staff in cooperation with the Department of Education and Regional School Operations. Their responsibilities include local input on the selection of principals and teachers and collaboration on staffing needs, while the Government of Nunavut remains responsible for territorial education administration and employment arrangements. The exact hiring role should be checked against the Education Act and current departmental procedures rather than assuming each DEA independently appoints all staff.

context_text: A Canadian patent based on an application filed Oct 1 1989 or later has a base 20-year term counted from filing date, not grant date. The term is subject to applicable maintenance fees, and additional term can apply under other provisions.
question: Pour un brevet canadien moderne, le délai de base de vingt ans se calcule-t-il à partir du dépôt ou de la délivrance?
reference_answer: À partir de la date de dépôt de la demande. L'article 44 de la Loi sur les brevets fixe la durée de base d'un brevet canadien issu d'une demande déposée le 1er octobre 1989 ou après à vingt ans à compter de ce dépôt, et non de la date de délivrance. Le maintien en vigueur, les éventuels ajustements prévus par la loi et les autres conditions applicables peuvent avoir une incidence sur la durée effective des droits.

context_text: A complete notification of a notifiable transaction normally triggers an initial 30-day statutory waiting period prohibiting closing. A supplementary information request creates second waiting period of 30 days after complete responses, subject to early clearance, orders or timing commitments.
question: Does notifying the Competition Bureau of a proposed merger mean the parties can close immediately?
reference_answer: No. For a merger subject to mandatory notification under Canada's Competition Act, submitting a complete notification generally starts an initial 30-day statutory waiting period during which the parties cannot complete the deal unless the Commissioner gives the applicable early-closing clearance. A supplementary information request can trigger a second 30-day waiting period after full responses are received, and interim orders or timing commitments may further affect closing.

context_text: Canadian Bill of Rights is federal statutory human-rights instrument enacted in 1960, not part of constitution. Canadian Charter is part of Constitution since 1982 and binds federal and provincial governments within section 32 applicability, enjoying constitutional supremacy.
question: La Déclaration canadienne des droits et la Charte ont-elles le même statut juridique?
reference_answer: Non. La Déclaration canadienne des droits de 1960 est une loi fédérale à caractère quasi constitutionnel, qui s'applique dans son champ d'application fédéral et peut protéger des droits dans ce cadre. La Charte canadienne des droits et libertés fait partie de la Constitution du Canada depuis 1982 : elle a donc un statut constitutionnel supérieur et vise les institutions fédérales et provinciales dans leurs compétences respectives. Les deux instruments ne sont ni juridiquement identiques ni interchangeables.

context_text: Qualified priority-entitled candidates are considered and appointed ahead of others under federal statutory/regulatory priority rules. Priority does not override essential job qualifications like language or security; statutory priority outranks regulatory priority.
question: What is a priority entitlement supposed to do in federal public service staffing?
reference_answer: A priority entitlement gives an eligible person a legally defined preference for appointment within the federal public service when they meet the position's essential qualifications and conditions of employment. It can apply to particular groups—for example some employees affected by workforce adjustment or qualifying medical release—and must be respected before ordinary candidates. It is not an unconditional promise of any job, nor does it waive essential language or security requirements; statutory priorities take precedence over regulatory priorities.

context_text: A serious deterioration in tenant health creating inability to remain in unit can justify early lease termination if prescribed conditions met. Normally use Form G with physician Form H, or institutional acceptance letter for special care, and serve landlord according to instructions.
question: En Nouvelle-Écosse, un problème de santé peut-il parfois permettre au locataire de mettre fin plus tôt à un bail à durée déterminée?
reference_answer: Oui. En Nouvelle-Écosse, une détérioration importante de la santé du locataire ou d'un membre de sa famille vivant dans le logement peut permettre de mettre fin à un bail, même à durée déterminée, lorsque les conditions des articles 10B ou 10C de la Residential Tenancies Act sont réunies. Il faut généralement donner au propriétaire au moins un mois de préavis à l'aide du formulaire G et joindre un certificat du médecin (formulaire H). Une admission dans un établissement de soins peut également ouvrir une autre voie. Un simple désagrément de santé ne suffit pas automatiquement.

context_text: Canada's audited consolidated financial statements for 2025 are in Public Accounts Volume I, Section 2. Volume II presents detailed expenses and revenues and Volume III supplementary analyses; neither is the consolidated statements section.
question: Where in the 2025 Public Accounts can I find Canada’s audited consolidated financial statements?
reference_answer: In the Public Accounts of Canada 2025, look in **Volume I, Section 2**, titled the audited consolidated financial statements of the Government of Canada. That section also forms part of the annual financial reporting audited by the Auditor General. Volume II contains departmental financial operations, while Volume III contains supplementary analyses, so neither replaces the consolidated statements in Volume I.

context_text: Federal budget accounting uses accrual while Estimates use modified cash basis. Timing and included fiscal items differ because accrual recognizes incurred expense rather than payment and the publications have different scope. Treasury Board's comparison explicitly states this.
question: Pourquoi les chiffres des crédits budgétaires fédéraux peuvent-ils différer de ceux des charges présentées selon la comptabilité d’exercice?
reference_answer: Le Budget des dépenses fédéral vise surtout les besoins de trésorerie et les autorisations de paiement que le Parlement doit approuver, selon une base de comptabilité de caisse modifiée. À l'inverse, les charges budgétaires présentées selon la comptabilité d'exercice sont reconnues lorsque les obligations ou les charges naissent, et non nécessairement lors du décaissement. Les deux documents ont aussi des périmètres différents : par exemple, certaines prestations législatives ou crédits d'impôt ne figurent pas comme crédits votés. Les chiffres peuvent donc différer par la période, la méthode comptable et les éléments couverts.

context_text: ESDC grants are subject to preset eligibility criteria and normally not detailed expenditure accounting by recipients, with possible exceptions. ESDC contributions require eligible costs/conditions and accounting and may undergo examination or audit.
question: What’s the practical difference between an ESDC grant and a contribution agreement?
reference_answer: An ESDC grant is generally a transfer to an eligible recipient based on predetermined criteria, without routine detailed accounting for exactly how every dollar was spent, although outcome reporting or program-specific checks may still apply. An ESDC contribution is conditional funding governed by an agreement, often reimbursing eligible expenditures and requiring the recipient to demonstrate compliance, results or spending. Neither category should be interpreted as money with no accountability whatsoever.

context_text: The minister must develop a federal sustainable development strategy at least once every three-year period under section 9(1). Designated entities contribute to development of the strategy and it sets measurable goals and targets; strategy frequency does not negate other reporting duties.
question: À quelle fréquence le gouvernement fédéral doit-il élaborer une stratégie de développement durable en vertu de la loi fédérale?
reference_answer: La Loi fédérale sur le développement durable prévoit, à son paragraphe 9(1), l'élaboration d'une nouvelle Stratégie fédérale de développement durable au moins une fois tous les trois ans. Cette obligation vise la stratégie fédérale et s'accompagne de contributions des entités désignées et d'un processus de consultation; elle ne signifie pas que chaque ministère peut attendre trois ans pour rendre compte de tous ses engagements environnementaux.

context_text: Eligible new Saskatchewan residents must apply for Saskatchewan Health Services Card for insured provincial health services. Eligibility and effective date depend on immigration status, residence and previous coverage; do not assume coverage on day of arrival.
question: I’m new to Saskatchewan. What provincial card should I apply for to access insured health services?
reference_answer: Apply for a **Saskatchewan Health Services Card** if you meet the province's eligibility rules. You can apply through eHealth Saskatchewan, which verifies your residence and identity. If you moved from another province or territory, the start of Saskatchewan coverage normally coordinates with the end of your former province's plan; if you moved from outside Canada or have a temporary immigration status, different eligibility and effective-date rules may apply. Do not assume a new card activates coverage on the day you arrive.

context_text: Saltwater fishing in Gwaii Haanas requires applicable federal Tidal Waters Fishing Licence. Freshwater fishing is not permitted in Gwaii Haanas, and marine closures, species limits and conservation zoning still apply.
question: Pour pêcher en eau salée à Gwaii Haanas, quel permis faut-il vérifier avant de partir?
reference_answer: Pour pêcher en eau salée dans la région de Gwaii Haanas, il faut vérifier et obtenir le permis fédéral de pêche dans les eaux de marée (Tidal Waters Fishing Licence) applicable en Colombie-Britannique. Consultez également les fermetures, restrictions d'espèces et zones de conservation marine en vigueur. Parcs Canada précise par ailleurs que la pêche en eau douce n'est pas autorisée à Gwaii Haanas; un permis de pêche maritime n'y permet donc pas la pêche en eau douce.

context_text: Section 10 prohibits introducing aquatic species into water frequented by fish outside their indigenous region without federal/provincial legal authorization. The prohibition applies to nonindigenous species generally, not solely species named in a separate invasive-species schedule.
question: Can I release a non-native aquatic species into a lake frequented by fish in Canada?
reference_answer: No, not without legal authorization. Section 10 of the federal Aquatic Invasive Species Regulations prohibits introducing an aquatic species into a region or body of water frequented by fish where that species is not indigenous, unless authorized under applicable federal or provincial law. The prohibition is not confined to species specifically named on an invasive-species schedule. Check relevant provincial requirements as well as the federal regulation before moving or releasing any organism.

context_text: A work meeting criteria for a minor work under Minor Works Order may proceed without prior CNWA approval application. Some minor works require deposit of information and public notice, and charted-water works may require Coast Guard notification.
question: Si mon projet répond aux critères d’un ouvrage mineur en eaux navigables, dois-je toujours demander une approbation à Transports Canada?
reference_answer: Non, pas nécessairement. Un projet qui respecte les critères techniques et les conditions de l'Arrêté sur les ouvrages mineurs peut être réalisé sans demande d'approbation préalable de Transports Canada au titre de la Loi sur les eaux navigables canadiennes. Cependant, certaines catégories d'ouvrages mineurs exigent tout de même le dépôt d'information au registre et la publication d'un avis public; d'autres avis, notamment à la Garde côtière, ou des autorisations environnementales peuvent être nécessaires.

context_text: Indian Act registration and Inuit land-claim-organization recognition are separate NIHB eligibility paths. Canadian residency is required, and some qualifying Inuit clients receive benefits through regional government/authority arrangements. Indigenous Services Canada's eligibility bullets list both separately.
question: Can a person qualify for the federal Non-Insured Health Benefits program as an Inuit client even if they aren’t registered under the Indian Act?
reference_answer: Yes. Recognition as an Inuk by an Inuit land-claim organization is a separate eligibility pathway for the federal Non-Insured Health Benefits (NIHB) program; Indian Act registration is not required for that pathway. The applicant must also be a Canadian resident and meet the program's other conditions. Some Inuit populations receive equivalent benefits administered directly by their regional Inuit government or authority, so the process and service provider differ by land-claim region and place of residence.

context_text: An enduring power of attorney gives an authorized attorney powers concerning an adult's financial, property and legal affairs, continuing despite incapacity. The document may authorize powers while capable or when incapacity occurs; effective-date/event and signing conditions are defined in section 26.
question: En Colombie-Britannique, à quoi sert une procuration perpétuelle dans la planification de l’inaptitude?
reference_answer: En Colombie-Britannique, une procuration perpétuelle (*enduring power of attorney*) permet à un adulte capable de désigner un mandataire pour gérer les affaires financières et juridiques visées dans le document, selon ses conditions. Elle peut prendre effet immédiatement ou seulement à la survenance de l'inaptitude, mais elle doit prévoir expressément que le pouvoir continue malgré l'inaptitude du mandant. Elle n'autorise pas, à elle seule, les décisions de soins personnels ou de santé, qui relèvent d'autres mécanismes.

context_text: Flin Flon has residential and commercial properties in both provinces. The official name occurs on both sides. Flin Flon lies on the Manitoba–Saskatchewan border.
question: Mon bail indique seulement « Flin Flon ». L’assureur me demande dans quelle province se trouve le logement. Est-ce que le nom de la ville suffit?
reference_answer: Non. Il y a des propriétés à Flin Flon des deux côtés de la frontière entre le Manitoba et la Saskatchewan. Vérifiez l’adresse complète du logement ou demandez au propriétaire de confirmer la province.
